Mason Mount’s availability for the trip to Hull is in the balance due to a knock.

Sports.title: Robot building and Essien: Yirenkyi’s circuitous path to Premier League
Sports.content:
It is mid-July in Kössen, an Austrian village on the edge of the Alps, close to the German border, at Nordsjælland’s pre-season camp. The Danish Superliga club’s coaching staff, including Michael Essien, are preparing for the new campaign, the stunning scenery par for the course. Every training session is recorded by a drone. The operator with the joystick in his hands? Well, that would be Caleb Yirenkyi, the Ghana midfielder who returned a week early from his post-World Cup break.

He requested to join his teammates in the drills, but after physios told the 20-year-old he required more rest Yirenkyi did the next best thing. It is a story that speaks volumes of his modest character and, a month on, he is poised to make his Premier League debut at Arsenal on Friday after Coventry made him their £26m record signing.

Months earlier, Frank Lampard discussed Yirenkyi with Essien, his former Chelsea teammate, and Coventry beat off competition from top-flight rivals to make him their player after Ghana’s last-32 exit in the United States.

Yirenkyi’s story is another triumph for Right to Dream (RTD), the academy umbrella that, via the Mansour Group, owns Nordsjælland. The club is based in Farum, north of Copenhagen, and developed Mohammed Kudus, Simon Adingra, Kamaldeen Sulemana and Ibrahim Osman. Mikkel Damsgaard and Patrick Dorgu progressed through Nordsjælland’s youth programme and, in recent years, RTD opened hubs in Egypt and the US. “We are very excited to see a player go directly from the Superliga to the biggest league,” says Alexander Riget, Nordsjælland’s director of football. “Last year there were seven or eight players who were developed in our academy in the Premier League but most of them took a ‘middle step’ before playing – Adingra went on loan to Union Saint-Gilloise, Kudus went to Ajax, Damsgaard played in Italy [for Sampdoria] – but this is different.”

Part of Yirenkyi’s appeal is that he is a versatile performer. After making his first senior start in February 2025, he started every league game for which he was available until departing this month, missing just three matches, all through suspension. He is predominantly a central midfielder but has played at right-back for his country and ended his time at Nordsjælland as a left centre-back.

At the start of last year, he excelled in a 3-1 victory over Manchester United in Altrincham (in front of a crowd of 334) en route to the Premier League International Cup quarter-finals, a tournament for under-21 teams. In Toronto this summer, Yirenkyi’s 95th-minute winner against Panama in Ghana’s Group L opener, a goal set up by his now Coventry teammate Brandon Thomas-Asante, made him only the second Ghanaian man to score on his World Cup debut, after Haminu Draman.

View image in fullscreen Caleb Yirenkyi in action for Nordsjælland. Photograph: Noah Thilemann/FC Nordsjælland

Yirenkyi idolised Essien growing up and Essien’s words of wisdom were priceless. “Sometimes I see some glimpses that remind me of myself when I was little,” Essien said this year. Lampard sees those parallels himself and also shades of N’Golo Kanté’s qualities; Yirenkyi won possession more times than any other player in the Superliga last season (205) and was crowned young player of the year.

Djimi Traoré, the former Liverpool defender, was another major influence. Traoré coached Yirenkyi at RTD in Ghana and quickly flagged his talent. Yirenkyi’s biggest challenge was learning how to harness his power. He initially joined Nordsjælland’s under-19s but regularly picked up yellow cards and was sometimes substituted to avoid the risk of reds. During a first-team camp in the Netherlands two years ago, Yirenkyi was pulled out of a training game because his desire to impose himself caused concerns he could injure key players a week before the new season.

Yirenkyi’s time with RTD was transformative. Born in the town of Bechem, he joined RTD in Kumasi aged nine and arrived in Denmark aged 18 from their academy hub in eastern Ghana, about two hours from Accra, the capital. Riget was Nordsjælland under-13s coach when he first came across Yirenkyi in Ghana. “At that point he was not one where you thought: ‘OK, he’s the next superstar,’ like you did with Kudus. He was a very disciplined student and it was not clear that he would be a professional footballer. At that time, Caleb was also very good at building robots.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Robots? Yirenkyi spent his free time studying robotics, an extracurricular activity while enrolled on RTD’s programme, which provides a pathway into football or further education scholarships. Such was Yirenkyi’s focus, teachers had to remind him to take a break. He won a national prize as a 13-year-old and only the Covid-19 pandemic prevented him from competing in the world championships in the US. After joining Coventry, he was asked what he would do if he were not a footballer? “I’d build robots,” came the reply. Flying the drone this summer, then, was a doddle.

Coventry have signed Yirenkyi for his ability on the pitch but his personality off it is equally endearing. “He is a guy for whom actions speak louder than words,” says Riget of a quiet, low-maintenance and introverted individual. On the morning after Coventry finalised a deal that would increase his salary about twentyfold, Yirenkyi was his usual self with teammates at breakfast. Three days earlier, in his final game for Nordsjælland, he was anything but winding down. “When players make these kinds of moves it can affect them a little, but we had a game against Randers where he was tackling with his head on the ground,” Riget says.

View image in fullscreen Caleb Yirenkyi pictured with one of his robot projects while playing at Right to Dream academy. Photograph: Right to Dream

There are plenty of tales that speak to Yirenkyi’s humility. While in Denmark, he stayed in Farum during the off-season to achieve peak condition, and in 2024 he spent Christmas Eve with the family of the transitions coach, Thomas Kristensen, a former Denmark midfielder. “They had 26 guests at their house and Caleb was number 27,” says Riget. “Thomas’s grandmother is 85 but because of Caleb she watched every FC Nordsjælland game and now she will follow him at Coventry.”

Yirenkyi was always last to leave the dressing room, last off the team bus, only doing so after making sure he and his teammates left no trace; Coventry’s kit staff already appreciate his help gathering loose balls at the end of sessions. “He has been a joy to work with in this short time,” Lampard said. “I think there is going to be a big, big uplift in this boy … we believe he is going to have a really good career.”

When Yirenkyi signed for Nordsjælland, he lived in one of 34 rooms on the club’s campus but, unlike most players who move out after a few months, he stayed until joining Coventry. “He just wanted to stay, use his bicycle and be a professional footballer,” says Riget. “Normally when players leave, we need to help them. But when our operations team went into Caleb’s room, it was empty, absolutely spotless and he had left flowers and a card. He is a special character, for sure.”

Sports.title: West Ham condemn ‘offensive and divisive’ chant about Israel winger Manor Solomon
Sports.content:
West Ham have condemned “an offensive and divisive chant” and urged fans not to sing it at their first Championship home game of the season against Charlton on Saturday.

The chant, which relates to their Israel winger Manor Solomon and includes an anti-Palestine message, was sung by a section of the away support during their game against Burnley on Sunday, which ended in a 2-2 draw.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

West Ham said: “We understand that singing and chanting is a traditional and deeply embedded part of the matchday experience. We encourage our supporters to sing loud and proud about their football club and the players wearing the claret and blue shirt, but never in a way that creates division or causes offence among fellow fans.



“We are immensely proud of the fact that West Ham United has always been an inclusive football club, ever since our formation in 1895 … in the 131 years that have followed, that identity has evolved with the club located in one of the most diverse and multicultural areas of London, always open and welcoming to those who become members of the West Ham family and share the values we cherish.



“Equality, equity, diversity and inclusion are at the heart of the club and we believe in the power of football to unite and bring people together. We expect those who represent the club – be that players, staff, officials or supporters – to share those values and ensure that, regardless of individual backgrounds or beliefs, we are as our name says: United. Let’s make sure our support is something to be proud of and the envy of all who face us.”

Solomon scored the Hammers’ second goal on his debut at Turf Moor. The 27-year-old winger moved from Tottenham this month for a reported £5m fee, having also played for Fulham and Leeds in England.



West Ham had a 2-0 lead after Solomon scored in the 72nd minute, but two goals from Zian Flemming, including an injury-time equaliser.

The West Ham manager, Nuno Espírito Santo, told BBC Radio London he was impressed with Solomon’s first outing for the club: “I was happy he scored. It will improve his confidence and he brings very good things [to us]. He is a very talented player.”

Sports.title: Liverpool have Bradley Barcola alternative staring them in the face and he is half the price
Sports.content:
Liverpool have Bradley Barcola alternative staring them in the face and he is half the price

Liverpool have the perfect Bradley Barcola alternative staring them in the face this summer, according to Andy Brassell.

He believes that Barcola's teammate Ibrahim Mbaye would represent a very handy option should a deal for Barcola not prove to be possible.

5 Barcola is set to depart Paris Saint-Germain this summer after a host of attacking arrivals Credit: AFP

talkSPORT understands that the French international wants to move to Anfield this summer.

However, the Reds are unwilling to match the asking price.

Paris Saint-Germain are asking for around £130million to part ways with Barcola despite the club signing a few new forwards.

Mbaye has reportedly agreed personal terms with Liverpool as well and could be part of a double deal.

But if not, Brassell feels as if Mbaye would make more sense than Barcola.

Speaking exclusively to talkSPORT.com's Lead Features Writer Joe Brophy, Brassell praised Mbaye.

He said: "I think he's an enormous young talent who needs to get out and play. And he won't do that in Paris."

When asked if a move to Liverpool made sense, he responded: "It could be. Although, obviously, if we frame it like that, replacing Salah directly, well, A, is impossible. But B, that's a lot of pressure to put on someone.

"In terms of the fact that they need a right-sided forward, I think they need a right-sided forward more than they need Bradley Barcola.

"Not that I think Bradley Barcola would be anything less than excellent for them. But, yeah, that's definitely the key spot that they need to replace. And obviously, they're going around the squad and making little upgrades.

"And really, I think Liverpool are still settling from last year's transfer window, which was a bit tumultuous, really.

"A lot more change than a lot of people expected. But, yeah, a right-side player and a right-side player of talent is exactly what they need."

5 Mbaye is a special young talent and full Senegalese international already

5 Barcola is still Liverpool's top target as the transfer window ticks towards its conclusion Credit: Getty

Double departure

PSG have signed three attacking players in the transfer window.

Maghned Akliouche has arrived from Monaco to slot in as an option on the right.

Mika Godts has swapped Ajax for Paris to be a left winger for Luis Enrique's side, and Ferran Torres has also come in.

So, some players need to leave, and Brassell can see both Barcola and Mbaye departing.

"Yeah, absolutely. And I don't think it's just down to the Trophy de Champions [where they were both out of the squad]. I think, really, if something has happened this weekend, to mean that it's in the best interest of everyone for Barcola and Mbaye to move, which I think it was anyway, it's the fact that you've got that incredible front three and then you've added Akliouche to that.

"And over this weekend, on Friday, they added Ferran Torres, officially, at last. And then they've added Mika Godts as well. So, that really squeezes the minutes for the other guys, I think. And that really indicates that PSG are ready to do business before the bell tolls on September 1st.

"And we've seen that PSG earlier in this window have sold very well. I think they'll continue to sell very well. That's a huge part of being an elite club, isn't it?"

5 Andoni Iraola is after some more attacking additions Credit: Getty

Mbaye's rise

Despite being just 18, Mbaye is already an established player for Senegal.

He has four goals for his country, including one during the 2026 World Cup.

Last year was his big breakthrough in Ligue 1 as he made 24 appearances for the French giants, racking up some very good minutes.

He grabbed three goals and two assists and also appeared in the Champions League four times as well.

So, he's had one year of first-team football, but the talent is undoubtedly there, and he is a right winger, which Liverpool absolutely need.

5 Mbaye is a top talent who could thrive in the Premier League Credit: Getty

Liverpool's transfer window so far

The Reds have seen a summer of upheaval.

Mohamed Salah and Andrew Robertson have departed the club, with Curtis Jones set to join them as well.

He's heading to Inter Milan, while Cody Gakpo continues to be linked with Tottenham Hotspur.

Ibrahima Konate also didn't sign a new contract and has joined Real Madrid.

Jeremy Jacquet has arrived to replace Konate, and Julian Araujo is in on loan from Barcelona.

And there has only been one further addition, with Victor Munoz joining from Osasuna.

So, plenty still to do for Andoni Iraola.

Sports.title: EFL player handed retrospective two-match ban after handball goal in first of its kind ruling
Sports.content:
EFL player handed retrospective two-match ban after handball goal in first of its kind ruling

West Brom striker Aune Heggebo has been handed a two-match ban by the FA in a 'first of its kind' ruling.

The forward has been suspended for 'successfully deceiving a match official' in his side's controversial 2-1 win over Norwich City.



4 Heggebo has been handed a two-match ban by the FA for his handball goal against Norwich Credit: Alamy

Heggebo scored the Baggies' opening goal in their away victory at Carrow Road on Saturday.

However, replays showed he had diverted Jimmy-Jay Morgan's cross into the net with his arms.

Despite the appeals of the Norwich players, the goal was allowed to stand by referee Tim Robinson.



The goal quickly went viral on social media, leading to calls for VAR to be introduced by the EFL.

FA statement

Following the incident, Heggebo was subsequently charged by the FA this week.



Despite West Brom appealing against their decision, he has been suspended for two matches with immediate effect.

Confirming the punishment in a statement, the FA spokesperson said: "West Bromwich Albion’s Aune Heggebo has been given a two-match ban for successful deception of a match official during their EFL Championship match against Norwich City on Saturday 15 August.



"It was alleged that the player acted in an improper manner in or around the 75th minute of the match, whereby he successfully deceived a match official by handling the ball in a direct and successful attempt to score a goal, contrary to FA Rule E3.1.

"Aune Heggebo denied the charge against him, however an independent Regulatory Commission found it to be proven and imposed this sanction following a hearing.

"The Regulatory Commission’s written reasons will be published in due course."

4 Heggebo was charged for 'successfully deceiving a match official' after scoring with his arms Credit: Getty



Heggebo will now miss Sunday's home match against Burnley, live on talkSPORT 2.

The 25-year-old will also be suspended for West Brom's trip to Newcastle United in the Carabao Cup second round on Wednesday.

He will be available to return to action away at Middlesbrough on Saturday, August 29.

West Brom statement

West Brom have released a statement of their own following the ban, confirming their plans to seek clarification from the FA.



The club will request guidance on how their players should react in future to avoid a repeat offence.

In a statement, the Baggies said: "The FA on Tuesday charged Heggebo with a breach of Rule E3.1 in relation to his goal at Norwich City on Saturday.

4 West Brom will seek clarity from the FA after an unsuccessful appeal against the charge Credit: Getty

"The charge is believed to be the first of its kind in English football, following a rule change prior to the 2024/25 season.



"The FA alleged Heggebo did 'successfully deceive a Match Official by handling the ball in a direct successful attempt to score a goal'.

"Albion appealed on Wednesday, stating the ball took a deflection from the goalkeeper immediately before making contact with Heggebo's arm, which materially affected the ball's trajectory and left him with less than 0.1 of a second to react.

"Given the accidental nature of the handball, the club argued it could not be reasonably viewed as a deliberate act of deception.

"On Thursday, the matter was placed before a Regulatory Commission, which upheld the charge.



"The club will now write to the FA requesting clarification on how a player is reasonably expected to react should similar circumstances arise in the future.

4 Heggebo will miss West Brom's matches against Burnley and Newcastle Credit: Getty

"Albion remain steadfast in their support of Aune, whose character and integrity have been evident throughout his time at The Hawthorns."

Heggebo joined the Baggies from Brann in his native Norway last summer.



He has since scored ten goals in 47 Championship appearances for the club.

James Morrison's side sit fourth in the second-tier following their opening weekend win over the Canaries.

Sports.title: Aston Villa have £20m bid to sign England international as potential Ezri Konsa replacement rejected
Sports.content:
Aston Villa have £20m bid to sign England international as potential Ezri Konsa replacement rejected

Aston Villa have had an £18million, plus £2m in add-ons bid for Taylor Harwood-Bellis rejected by Southampton, talkSPORT understands.

Villa are looking to sign a new centre-back before the end of the summer transfer window on September 1 as Ezri Konsa is on course to leave.



2 Villa's first offer is some £10million below Southampton's valuation of the player Credit: Getty

Premier League champions Arsenal are understood to have verbally agreed a deal worth £50m to sign the 28-year-old.

Tosin Adarabioyo and Fikayo Tomori are among a list of centre-back targets for Villa.

Another option is Harwood-Bellis, although an initial offer has been rebuffed with Saints valuing him at £30m.



Harwood-Bellis is a graduate of the Manchester City academy before making a permanent move to Southampton in 2024.

He initially joined on loan for the 2023/24 season, with his move then made permanent for a £20m fee after promotion to the top flight.



Harwood-Bellis, who is engaged to and is set to have a child with Roy Keane's daughter Leah, has made 134 appearances in defence for the Saints and been captain on numerous occasions.

The 24-year-old is also an England international as he earned his sole cap and scored against the Republic of Ireland in November 2024.



Who have Villa sold this summer?

Villa have experienced a summer of big change, despite winning the Europa League at the end of last season.

Youri Tielemans, Morgan Rogers and Lucas Digne are among the key departures for Unai Emery's side.

Ollie Watkins has been linked with a sensational move to Saudi club Al Hilal, and Emi Martinez could still leave amid a failed transfer to Juventus.

2 Konsa looks to be heading to Arsenal after seven seasons at Villa Credit: Getty



Should the pair exit Villa Park along with Konsa, then only five of the starting XI that beat SC Freiburg in the Europa League will be left.

They would be Matty Cash, Pau Torres, Victor Lindelof, John McGinn and Emi Buendia.

However, Villa have been active in terms of incomings, with Swiss star Johan Manzambi joining in a £51.2m move from Freiburg.

Joao Gomes then joined from West Midlands rivals Wolves for £35m.

On Wednesday, Villa completed the signings of Matteo Ruggeri and Zion Zuzuki.



The former has arrived from Atletico Madrid, whilst the latter signed from Parma.

Sports.title: Brighton CEO refuses to comment Manchester United’s pursuit of Carlos Baleba
Sports.content:
Brighton chief executive Paul Barber has confirmed the world's biggest clubs have shown interest in Carlos Baleba.

However, he refused to comment when asked about Manchester United's pursuit of the midfielder.



3 United are in advanced talks with Brighton over a deal for Baleba Credit: Getty

talkSPORT revealed on Wednesday that the Red Devils are in advanced talks with Brighton to sign Baleba.

It comes after a bid worth an initial £60million plus £5million in add-ons was placed for the 22-year-old.

United are confident of reaching an agreement with the Seagulls before the transfer window closes.



Baleba has already agreed to the move with personal terms in place.

Brighton CEO on Baleba interest

Barber joined White and Jordan live on talkSPORT on Thursday ahead of Brighton's Conference League play-off against Tromso.

When asked by Jim White if Baleba is joining United, though, he refused to comment on the transfer.



Instead, he replied: "It’s not something that I can talk about right now.

"This time of year we’re always going to be subject to bids for our players, we’re always going to be interested in ones that are sensible and are going to make sense for us financially, economically.



"But we also have to balance that with making sure our squad is as strong as it can be to compete in competitions like the one we’re in.

"So nothing really to say on Carlos at the moment other than that he’s a hugely talented young midfielder who’s done really well for us and has attracted interest from some of the biggest clubs in the world now for a couple of years."

3 Barber has revealed Baleba has attracted interest from some of the world's biggest clubs Credit: Alamy

Baleba has made 112 appearances for Brighton since joining the club from Lille in 2023.



The Cameroon international currently currently has just under two years remaining on his contract, although there is an option for a further 12 months.

United are also unfazed by an ankle injury suffered by Baleba in pre-season.

As a result of the setback, Baleba was absent from the Brighton squad for their trip to Norway to face Tromso.

Brighton stars in demand

The Seagulls' former Young Player of the Season is not the only one of their stars wanted by a Premier League rival.



Liverpool have seen a £50million bid for Yankuba Minteh rejected by Brighton.

3 Liverpool are interested in Minteh despite the fact he's nursing a leg injury Credit: Getty

talkSPORT previously revealed the Reds' interest in the winger back in June.

Minteh is currently sidelined until October with a leg injury suffered in a friendly against Roma earlier this month.



Following their eighth place finish last season, Brighton have already lost two key men this summer.

Defender Jan Paul van Hecke has moved to Tottenham Hotspur, whilst Chelsea swooped to complete a cut-price deal for Danny Welbeck.

Sports.title: Brazilian sources expecting imminent Endrick bid from Premier League giants
Sports.content:
Liverpool are poised to make a move for Real Madrid starlet Endrick, according to sources in Brazil.

South American football expert Tim Vickery told talkSPORT a substantial bid from the Reds for the 20-year-old striker is being rumoured.

3 Endrick featured for Brazil at this summer's World Cup Credit: Getty

Is an Endrick exit on the cards?

Endrick joined Real Madrid from Brazilian club Palmeiras in 2024 after a £51m deal was initially agreed in 2022, but he saw his opportunities limited last term and he ended up spending the second half of the season on loan at Lyon.

So, could he be on his way to the Premier League before the end of the transfer window?

Vickery said on Hawksbee and Jacobs: "Well, it's interesting that we've just been hearing about the victory of the lost king – probably everyone paying tribute to Kevin Keegan this weekend at Liverpool, and the loss of Mo Salah.

"Is Endrick going to be an attempt at the found king? Well, we shall see. I have my doubts.

"Not least because – and this is getting a lot of traction in Brazil at the moment...– Liverpool are apparently preparing an offer – big-money offer – but the fee that's being reported that Liverpool want to offer is less than Real Madrid for him a couple of years ago.

"Now, he hasn't been a failure at all, and the problem with Real Madrid is he went to a club that didn't need him – but his numbers even with Real Madrid aren't bad.

"And he did very well on loan with Lyon, so there's no way that he can be worth less than he was as an 18-year-old when Real Madrid bought him. So, that is, I think, problem number one.

"How high are Liverpool prepared to go? And would Real Madrid want to sell him to a competitor in the Champions League?"

Endrick's surprising idol

Vickery also pondered whether Endrick's admission of idolising a Manchester United icon would be well-received by Liverpool fans.

He continued: "One possible problem is, you know who one of his idols is? This is going to shock you; oh, I'm looking forward to this.

3 Endrick has scored seven goals for Real Madrid so far Credit: Getty

"Endrick, 20 years of age, one of his idols is... Ta-da! Bobby Charlton. Yes, yes, Bobby Charlton.

"You remember he scored a goal for Brazil. He scored the winner against England at Wembley just over two years ago...and he was saying, talking to Brazilian media afterwards, 'I'm delighted to have scored a goal in the place where, the very stadium where Bobby Charlton [starred for England and Man United].

"Is that going to go down well with the Kop and the Annie [Anfield] Road faithful?"

Vickery also highlighted Endrick's need to play in a front two, a system new Liverpool head coach Andoni Iraola hasn't tended to deploy.

"I don't know," he went on. "He is a wonderfully talented player – really, really good player – but he does suffer, I think, a little bit from a question which I think affects a lot of players in his position – which is what exactly is his position?

"Can we go back to Kevin Keegan – [John] Toshack and Keegan? You know where you stood for the old 4-4-2 – big man in, a little man in; the little man is a second striker.

3 Endrick scored his first Brazil goal against England at Wembley aged 17 Credit: Getty

"I think ideally, he's probably that second striker, but a lot of these new-fangled modern-day formations, it's quite hard for that old second striker in a 4-4-2 to kind of define himself."

Liverpool look ahead to big kick-off

Liverpool have so far only made two signings as they prepare for the start of the Iraola era, bringing in centre-back Jeremy Jacquet in a deal that was arranged in January as well as winger Victor Munoz.

However, the Reds continue to be linked with a huge deal for Paris Saint-Germain and France star Bradley Barcola.

talkSPORT also understands they recently had an offer to sign Brighton winger Yankubah Minteh rejected.

Liverpool kick off the new Premier League campaign away to Newcastle on Sunday.

Sports.title: Liverpool have £50m bid for injured Premier League winger rejected
Sports.content:
Liverpool have seen a £50million offer for Brighton and Hove Albion winger Yankuba Minteh turned down, talkSPORT understands.

The approach from the Reds was immediately rebuffed by the Seagulls, and Liverpool are now contemplating a second bid for the currently injured forward.

2 Minteh has established himself as a dangerous winger Credit: Getty

Liverpool are looking to add some more wingers before the end of the transfer window.

Should they acquire Minteh before the September 1 deadline, he wouldn't be immediately available for them as he's currently nursing a leg injury, which could keep him out for up to three months.

The Reds have signed Victor Munoz, but are yet to replace Mohamed Salah on the right.

They've been linked with Paris Saint-Germain star Bradley Barcola, although the France international's preferred position is on the left wing.

As well as Minteh, Ibrahim Mbaye is also on Liverpool's list.

The 18-year-old Senegalese international is likely to see his game time become very limited in France.

This is because PSG have signed Maghnes Akliouche, Mika Godts and Ferran Torres.

Minteh's Premier League statistics

Minteh was bought by Brighton from Newcastle United without the winger making an appearance in black and white.

He was sold in the summer of 2024 to the Seagulls following a loan with Feyenoord.

In his first year, the Gambian international scored six goals and set up a further four.

Last year, the 22-year-old added three more goals and four further assists.

Not outstanding statistics in any way, but the winger is a constant ball of energy, always on the move and always looking to create and get shots off.

However, his injury could prove to be a problem.

The forward limped off during Brighton's pre-season friendly against Roma and has now been ruled out until potentially November.

2 Iraola is hoping for some attacking additions before the close of the transfer window Credit: Getty

More needed

Andoni Iraola has only seen three first-team signings arrive this summer.

And Reds legend Phil Thompson believes that the Liverpool board need to be very busy in the remainder of the window.

Speaking on Footy Accumulator's No Tippy Tappy Football podcast, he said: "Defensively, we do need more. It is a particular area if Jacquet isn't fully ready, who is going to be there? It's a difficult one. We still need recruitment.

"I think we probably need four, maybe five players in total in different positions. Defensively, certainly, a midfield player, a wide player; you need two quality players for every position. There's work to be done."

What have they done so far?

As of now, Liverpool have signed two centre-backs.

Jeremy Jacquet has come in from Rennes to replace Ibrahima Konate.

Julian Araujo has joined from Barcelona on loan with an option to buy to provide cover.

And Munoz was picked up from Osasuna after the Reds activated his release clause.

They start their Premier League campaign off against Newcastle United at St James' Park on Sunday.

Sports.title: Mikel Arteta reveals Myles Lewis-Skelly’s Arsenal future has been decided
Sports.content:
Mikel Arteta has emphatically declared that Myles Lewis-Skelly will remain at Arsenal beyond the summer.

It was reported last week how the versatile Hale End graduate had been offered to Chelsea and Manchester United.



3 Lewis-Skelly starred in his last Arsenal outing to help them win the Community Shield Credit: Getty

Both clubs had previously been made aware of Lewis-Skelly's potential availability, with United showing interest in a move.

The 19-year-old's role in the squad this season had been questioned following the £75million arrival of Bruno Guimaraes.

Arteta didn't pour cold water on the exit rumours as he stated it is a 'good sign' that his players are linked with moves to other clubs.



Gunners supporters are desperate for the teenager to not be sold, with the England international establishing himself as a firm fan favourite.

Even former Newcastle and Crystal Palace boss Alan Pardew urged the Premier League champions to not sell the youngster - insisting it would be 'unforgivable'.



Lewis-Skelly once again showcased his supreme talent in his recent outing for Arsenal - just as he had done in the latter stages of the 2025/26 season.

Starting in Sunday's Community Shield victory over Manchester City, Lewis-Skelly expertly created Riccardo Calafiori's opener inside 25 seconds.



What has Mikel Arteta said about Myles Lewis-Skelly's Arsenal future?

Speaking ahead of Friday's Premier League opener at home to newly-promoted Coventry - live on talkSPORT - Arteta was asked in his press conference as to whether Lewis-Skelly will remain at the club.

To which he simply stated: "100 per cent."

Arteta was then pressed on whether Arsenal may have to follow suit like many of their top-flight rivals in recent years and sell their academy graduates.

3 Lewis-Skelly started just five Premier League games term from his 25 outings Credit: Getty

Like Lewis-Skelly, Ethan Nwaneri has been tipped to leave north London on a possible loan spell away following his stint at Marseille.



He was left out of the matchday squad for the Community Shield, with it expected he will be shipped out before the window slams shut.

Commenting on Arsenal's academy graduates, Arteta remarked: "The players that have been raised in our system, and they feel generally that love and that connection with the club, bring something else, there's no question about that.

"We need to look after them in a really special way because they bring value that is very difficult to find.

That's why, when we can, we want to protect those assets as much as possible, develop them and make them extremely important for the club."



And Arteta was also pressed on the difficulty of selling cult heroes, with Gabriel Martinelli and Gabriel Jesus believed to be up for sale.

3 Brazilian duo Martinelli and Jesus could be sold before the window closes Credit: Getty

To which the Spaniard remarked: "It's a really, really tough moment. We need to face that reality.

"But I think you need to face it with a real honesty and transparency because when you are on the other side, that's exactly what you need.



"You might not like what you've been told, but if it's truthful, if it's the reality, if it's honest and it's going to help you to make better decisions and have more clarity for the next steps in your career, you have to do that.

"These are always very difficult conversations, but they need to be done.

"It's like when a player doesn't feel that he belongs or he's important. He wants to have a different chapter. I think that communication has to exist and it has to be both ways.

"We all know that at the end, everything has a start and has an end.

"When it comes to the end, I think our duty, our responsibility is to do it in the best possible way, maintaining the respect and admiration for the player and the relationship, but understanding that at the end, we need to make football decisions."

Sports.title: Ronaldinho to come out of retirement at age 46 for third-tier Italian club
Sports.content:
Ronaldinho to come out of retirement at age 46 for third-tier Italian club

Brazilian icon Ronaldinho is set to come out of retirement and sign for Italian Serie C side Ravenna, aged 46.

The World Cup and Ballon d'Or-winning superstar had hung up his boots back in 2018 after a brief spell with Fluminense in 2015.



3 Ronaldinho starred alongside Ronaldo and Rivaldo as Brazil lifted the World Cup in 2002 Credit: AFP

But The Athletic report that he has arrived in Italy to resume his career, with 6,000 fans expected to greet him at a launch event on the nearby Adriatic coast.

Ronaldinho also becomes part of the club's ownership group fronted by Ignazio Cipriani, head of luxury hospitality business Mr. C Hotels & Residencies, having previously come onboard to help with Ravenna's marketing.

And the ex-Barcelona star has addressed doubts that he might not actually play for the club.



He told Flashscore: "I will certainly play a few minutes in an official match, then we’ll see how I feel."

Cipriani confirmed as much, explaining: "He has also chosen to make an extraordinary gift to the city and to his new club.



"He will take to the pitch for Ravenna in an official professional match, with one clear and romantic aim — to try to score the final goal of his career."

Who are Ravenna, Ronaldinho's new club?

Ravenna currently play in Group B of Serie C, the regionalised third tier of Italian football.



Nicknamed the Giallorossi, they are managed by former Inter Milan defender Andrea Mandorlini.

Having finished third in the table last season, Ravenna will begin the new Serie C campaign away to Reggiana on Monday.

That's after they were knocked out of the Coppa Italia in the last 32 earlier this month.

3 Ronaldinho scored almost 100 goals during a memorable five-year stint at Barcelona Credit: Getty



What has Ronaldinho achieved in his career?

Widely regarded as one of the greatest players of all time, Ronaldinho enjoyed a glittering career for club and country.

A key part of a star-studded Brazil's 2002 World Cup success, he earned 97 international caps between 1997 and 2013, scoring 33 goals.

Dubbed 'The Wizard', Ronaldinho regularly produced moments of stunning individual brilliance, spending his prime years at the Nou Camp.

There, he won two LaLiga titles and the Champions League title in 2006.



Bestowed with the ultimate individual honour of the Ballon d'Or in 2005, he was also named FIFA World Player of the year twice (back-to-back in 2004 and 2005).

He is one of only 11 players to win the Ballon d'Or, Champions League and World Cup, with Spain captain Rodri joining the list this summer.

3 Ronaldinho lifted the Champions League title in 2006 after beating Arsenal Credit: AFP

Having started out at hometown club Gremio, Ronaldinho also turned out for Paris Saint-Germain, AC Milan, Flamengo, Atletico Mineiro, Queretaro and Fluminense during his original playing days.



During his three-year stay in Milan, Ronaldinho lifted the Serie A title in 2011.

In 2004, he was named by fellow Brazilian legend Pele in his FIFA 100 list of the greatest living footballers at the time.

And in 2012, he even had the more curious distinction of having a species of bee named after him.

Sports.title: Liverpool expected to make improved offer for Brighton for winger Yankuba Minteh after £50m bid was rejected - with club still locked in talks with PSG in deal for Bradley Barcola
Sports.content:
Liverpool expected to make improved offer for Brighton for winger Yankuba Minteh after £50m bid was rejected - with club still locked in talks with PSG in deal for Bradley Barcola

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Liverpool are expected to make an improved offer for Brighton winger Yankuba Minteh after having a £50m bid rejected.

The Gambian is out until October after undergoing surgery on his right leg.

Liverpool reverted to the 22-year-old after considering Ibrahim Mbaye of Paris St Germain too expensive. They are continuing discussions for Bradley Barcola.

Daily Mail Sport reported upon Mohamed Salah’s departure that the Gambia international would feature on a list to bolster the wide forward position this summer.

While talks for Barcola are ongoing, they would preferably like two forwards with Ibrahim Mbaye, also of PSG, one sounded out last week.

Minteh is currently on the sidelines after suffering an injury in Brighton's pre-season win over Roma earlier this month.

Liverpool have approached Brighton over signing winger Yankuba Minteh this summer

Andoni Iraola's side are in the market to sign two forwards, with the club locked in talks over PSG's Bradley Barcola

Minteh has made 73 appearances for Brighton to date since joining from Newcastle in a £30m move in the summer of 2024. He has scored 10 goals and provided nine assists for the Seagulls.

Minteh predominantly plays on the right wing, but has also been used on the left by Fabian Hurzeler.

Meanwhile, Curtis Jones will have a medical at noon on Friday after Liverpool agreed to sell him to Inter Milan for £26.7m plus £4m in bonuses and a 10 percent sell-on.

The six-time England international, who joined Liverpool aged nine, has had his heart set on a move to Serie A for some time after failing to regularly establish himself as a starter at Anfield.

Liverpool are preparing for their first season under new manager Andoni Iraola, who replaced Arne Slot following the Dutchman's dismissal at the end of last season.

After spending over £450million on new signings including Alexander Isak, Florian Wirtz and Hugo Ekitike last summer, the 2024-25 Premier League champions struggled to reach the same heights again under the Dutchman and only narrowly managed to qualify for the Champions League with a fifth-place finish last term.

Liverpool, who waved farewell to Mohamed Salah, Andrew Robertson and Ibrahima Konate at the start of the summer, have so far recruited centre-half Jeremy Jacquet from Stade Rennais and left winger Victor Munoz from Osasuna ahead of the new campaign.

Sports.title: PREMIER LEAGUE PREDICTIONS: Our experts pick which side will win title, who will go down, biggest flop and best new signing ahead of the new season
Sports.content:
It's been a long 12 weeks since the final day of the 2025-26 season but football fans can finally rejoice - the Premier League is back.

With a bang, too. Liverpool, Manchester City, Chelsea, and Newcastle are just a clutch of the boldfaced names with new managers to keep an eye on, and anticipation is rising to see the summer rebuilds clubs have ushered in.

Now, on the eve of the return of top-flight football, Daily Mail Sport experts Oliver Holt, Ian Herbert, Mike Keegan, Kieran Gill, Lewis Steele and make their final predictions.

Tip to win the Premier League

Oliver Holt: Arsenal – they have made two good signings over the summer so far and sold prudently. They have strengthened from a position of strength. They look like a side that will be liberated by the confidence of being champions.

Ian Herbert: Arsenal - crossing the Rubicon to claim the title means so much, removes so much pressure. An excellent transfer window has made them stronger

Arsenal have got the devil off their back by wining their first Premier League title under Mikel Arteta and look stronger than ever

Chelsea welcome Xabi Alonso to Stamford Bridge unburdened by European football and having made key summer signings

Mike Keegan: Chelsea. We saw last season what an absence of European football can do at Manchester United and I like what I have seen at Stamford Bridge this summer given their recruitment pivot. The manager is top class and the old heads they have brought in could be enough for a stunning title assault.

Riath Al-Samarrai: Arsenal. They have the best squad, the least turbulence and have dismantled the mental barriers that previously dominated these conversations. The team to beat.

Kieran Gill: Arsenal. They are more settled than everyone else with Manchester City, Liverpool and Chelsea going through transitions under new managers. I’m not sure it will even be a close title race.

Lewis Steele: Arsenal. Best team by a distance last season. Manchester City were only close because the Gunners kept on stumbling and keeping them alive. Now, Mikel Arteta’s men will not have the tag of ‘bottlers’ or ‘chokers’ and that will free them up. I’d not be surprised if they won by 10 or more points.

Matt Barlow: Arsenal. Long time since they won back-to-back but strong and stable with main rivals in various degrees of flux. Bruno Guimaraes will improve them. Confident in the knowledge they have what it takes. Free from the anxiety of old.

Bobby Manzi: Arsenal appear stronger than last season, so this will no doubt be proved foolish come the end of the season. But Chelsea have an intelligent manager, have added experience to their squad and no European football to contend with - enabling them to focus on domestic glory. Alonso, against all odds, won the league invincible at Bayer Leverkusen. Chelsea look a good outside bet.

Completing the top four

Oliver Holt: Liverpool, Manchester City, Chelsea. For different reasons, Florian Wirtz and Alexander Isak had disappointing seasons with Liverpool last season. Both can flourish this year and Liverpool have new signings to complement them. Chelsea have a first class manager, no European commitments and a more realistic recruitment policy. City have the muscle-memory of previous greatness.

Ian Herbert: Chelsea, Tottenham, Manchester United. Something about Roberto de Zerbi’s energy allied to the big spending makes me think Spurs will be a big story this season. Chelsea on the up, too, but transition time for Manchester City and Liverpool

Mike Keegan: Arsenal will not be far off. You can’t judge City on a Community Shield but, for me, the jury remains firmly out on Enzo Maresca. Liverpool will improve under Andoni Iraola.

Alexander Isak endured a difficult first season at Liverpool but will be a major weapon fully fit

Riath Al-Samarrai: Liverpool, Manchester City, Chelsea. I don’t envision any of them making a sustained run on Arsenal, but a lot will depend on how quickly Liverpool adapt to Iraola’s style. That’s typically a slow process and a rapid finish. I can see them leading the chase.

Kieran Gill: Chelsea in second, City in third, Liverpool in fourth. Perhaps I’m thinking a tad optimistically on behalf of Xabi Alonso, but he is a good manager who has wielded his influence this summer.

Lewis Steele: Liverpool. People are sleeping on the ability of a much-improved Alexander Isak and Florian Wirtz. Their XI is very good but beyond that, it is a worry. Manchester City because they have a deep squad and did not deserve the overreaction or ridicule that came after losing a glorified friendly but losing Pep Guardiola, Bernardo Silva, Rodri and John Stones in the same summer rips their heart out. I’ll go with Chelsea in fourth as I like Xabi Alonso.

Matt Barlow: Chelsea, Liverpool, and Man City. I'm expecting Xabi Alonso to get a tune out of the mass of talent at Chelsea, Liverpool’s big signings from 2025 to improve and City to fade post-Pep Guardiola and post-Rodri but still have lots of quality and Erling Haaland’s goals.

Bobby Manzi: Arsenal, Man United, Man City. Arsenal are nailed on for the top two but will find the first couple of weeks without William Saliba difficult. Manchester United have executed intelligent summer business - they had to improve their midfield and they have. Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos and Carlos Baleba are a great blend. As long as Michael Carrick was not a one-hit wonder, they will be up there. A new era at Manchester City but they still have a strong squad to creep into the top four.

The three going down

Oliver Holt: Newcastle almost got sucked into a relegation battle last season. Since then, they’ve lost their biggest asset, Eddie Howe, and their three best players, Anthony Gordon, Bruno Guimaraes and Sandro Tonali. Their Saudi owners appear to have disconnected. I like Gary O’Neil, the Ipswich boss, but Ipswich are a classic yo-yo club. And I don’t think Hull have enough to stay up.

Ian Herbert: Fulham, Coventry and Ipswich. Fulham seem a perfect storm: inexperienced new manager, good players have left, an attempt to introduce new system to a club lacking intensity last season. There’s a bond about Hull City. I suspect they’ll be OK.

Newcastle have seen their ranks depleted and a successful manager depart ahead of the start of the season

Mike Keegan: Sunderland, Ipswich Town, Hull City. I’ll probably be the only one predicting Sunderland and I wish I wasn’t because they’re a great club with great fans but they massively overachieved last season and European football this time around could be a killer.

Riath Al-Samarrai: Hull, Ipswich, Fulham. That’s putting a certain amount of faith in Coventry, but Fulham have lost a strong manager and their best player in Harry Wilson. I think they’ll struggle.

Kieran Gill: Ipswich, Hull, Sunderland. I have a hunch that Coventry under Frank Lampard will surprise us, while Sunderland may struggle juggling European football with everything else.

Lewis Steele: Going to be boring and say the three promoted teams. I do think Sunderland will struggle from a bit of second-season syndrome but I think they have just enough quality with Enzo Le Fee, Granit Xhaka, Brian Brobbey et al.

Matt Barlow: Ipswich, Hull, Coventry. Those coming up can all take inspiration from last season’s survivors and there some established teams should be worried by the radical summer of change including Newcastle, Fulham and Palace but the gap still yawns.

Bobby Manzi: Coventry, Hull, Ipswich. Quite simply, the promoted sides are not better than any of the other 17 sides. Coventry have the best chance of staying up but they are lacking in defence.

The biggest overachievers will be

Oliver Holt: Spurs – they have bought well in the summer and in Roberto de Zerbi, they have one of the best managers of this generation. Like Chelsea, they have no European football to drain their resources. They’ll put their recent struggles behind them in style although they could do with a new striker.

Ian Herbert: Everton - drab end to last season obscured the way that David Moyes, such a fine and still underrated manager, has rescued them from annual purgatory. Some good recruits this summer. Moyes buys well. Europe calls.

Mike Keegan: Chelsea, followed by Coventry, who I think will defy the odds and stay up.

Riath Al-Samarrai: Brentford. Again. A smart club with a smart plan and they haven’t been raided quite like Brighton, who would be my second choice if they didn’t have to content with European commitments.

Kieran Gill: I may have hinted at this in my previous answer, but I’ll plump for Coventry. I’m not saying they will suddenly secure Europe. That’s a stretch. Somewhere towards the midtable would be cool.

Lewis Steele: A Brighton or Bournemouth could really flourish but may be held back by Europe. After finishing 17th twice in a row, lowly relegation fodder Spurs might climb up the table…

Tottenham have recruited intensely over the summer, luring Sandro Tonali from Newcastle in a bid to avoid a third 17th-place finish in three seasons

Matt Barlow: Leeds - finished last season at a gallop and reinforced in the summer market. Three winnable home fixtures to start at fortress Elland Road can build a platform for a strong season as others from mid table tackle complications of Europe

Bobby Manzi: Brentford. They were so close to Europe last season - missing out on goal difference. Many tipped them to go down under Keith Andrews and they defied expectation. This season, they may just get Europe. With Bournemouth, Crystal Palace, Sunderland and Brighton all playing on Thursday nights, the teams in the middle of the pack could suffer a drop-off in the league. Brentford have kept the majority of their squad from last season together and added sprinkles of quality such as Mamadou Sangare in midfield. They appear well positioned.

The biggest underachievers will be…

Oliver Holt: Manchester City – I know I’ve got City down to finish in my top four but I don’t think they’ll challenge for the title. It’s always tough when a great manager leaves a club after a long time in charge and I don’t think it will be any different for City. It’s a huge test for Enzo Maresca.

Ian Herbert: Newcastle – car crash summer from a club the Saudis couldn’t be bothered to administer properly, now led by a managerial novice. You’re well out of it, Eddie.

Mike Keegan: Manchester United. There is time left in the transfer window for United to strengthen but, as things stand, I do not think they have made the additions which will deliver another Champions League finish.

Riath Al-Samarrai: A three-way tie between Manchester United (thin squad), Newcastle (decimated squad and technical area) and Aston Villa (great expectations after last season but a pretty horrible summer of departures).

Kieran Gill: Aston Villa. As good of a manager as Unai Emery is, Villa have sold some big names this summer, from Morgan Rogers to Lucas Digne to Youri Tielemens, so I’m concerned they may struggle.

Aston Villa have seen their squad stripped of a number of key talents and have European tests to come later in the season

Lewis Steele: Newcastle. The bubble has burst. I did think it was probably right for Eddie Howe to move on but losing Sandro Tonali, Bruno Guimaraes and Anthony Gordon in the same window stinks.

Matt Barlow: Aston Villa. Challenging season ahead for Unai Emery. Lost Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans and Lucas Digne. Ezri Konsa leaving. Emi Martinez and Ollie Watkins unsettled. Key staff gone, too. And has a Champions League campaign to plot.

Bobby Manzi: Bourmemouth. It’s only natural to have a comedown after last season, finishing sixth on 57 points and securing Europa League football for the first time. Much like with Palace last season, playing Thursday-Sunday will take its toll domestically. A bottom-half finish but a strong European return for the Cherries.

Player of the season

Oliver Holt: There are early signs that Arsenal may have cast off the nerves that afflicted them last season. If they play with more freedom and justify their tag as favourites, Bukayo Saka may rediscover his best form.

Ian Herbert: Declan Rice was the orchestrator and architect of so much about Arsenal last season. I can see him running a side that’s feeling mentally released and free.

Mike Keegan: Cole Palmer. A summer off is incredibly rare in this world of saturated football and the mysteriously-omitted England winger will have a barnstormer.

Riath Al-Samarrai: Easy answer would be Haaland, again, but I’ll go with Odegaard at Arsenal. He looks fit and sharp again, which wasn’t always the case last season, but it’ll be interesting to see how Arteta constructs the puzzle with Rice and Guimaraes (who might well be the star turn – the guy can do everything).

Cole Palmer has had a summer off after an injury-stricken season and should be raring to go

Kieran Gill: Joao Pedro. Just because of what I’ve seen of him in Chelsea’s handful of pre-season games. He’s looking like a superstar, and it is understood he is set to sign a new contract.

Lewis Steele: Since I cover Liverpool I will keep my regular readers happy by going with Isak. I’ll look silly when he does his hamstring on Sunday.

Matt Barlow: Alexander Isak. Back to full fitness after his awful first season at Liverpool and sure to enjoy Andoni Iraola’s full throttle style.

Bobby Manzi: Erling Haaland. Goals, goals, goals. At the World Cup, Haaland proved he can find the back of the net regardless of who is around him - scoring seven in five matches. He’s a machine. Nobody will get close to him.

Signing of the summer (so far)

Oliver Holt: Jordan Henderson – not just because he still retains much of the quality he had in his prime but because he is a symbol of a change in approach that Chelsea desperately needed. Xabi Alonso has some brilliant young players at his disposal but it has to be leavened with experience and Henderson and Danny Welbeck are fine professionals who will provide that.

Ian Herbert: Bruno Guimaraes will look even classier in a world class midfield and his presence will free up Rice. Some tandem they’ll be. The £75m salary may come to look excellent value.

Mike Keegan: Youri Tielemans. For the first time in a long time, Manchester United have signed a player who looks like a Manchester United player. I think he’ll settle quickly at Old Trafford and a much-needed all-round presence in midfield.

Riath Al-Samarrai: Harry Wilson to Leeds for nothing.

Kieran Gill: Arsenal’s £75m landing of Bruno Guimaraes from Newcastle. He should fit into that midfield beside Declan Rice and Martin Odegaard nicely.

Bruno Guimaraes represents a coup for Arsenal's recruitment after his move from Newcastle

Lewis Steele: I like some of the low-key ones like Joao Gomes to Aston Villa and Ousmane Diomande to Nottingham Forest and Antonio Silva to Bournemouth. But for the sake of picking one I’ll go Matheus Fernandes.

Matt Barlow: Maxence Lacroix. Should bring much needed leadership and maturity to the heart of Chelsea’s young team and not bad value in today’s world of head-spinning fees.

Bobby Manzi: Youri Tielemans. Manchester United have been gradually improving their squad to mount a title charge by 2028. Last season they bought a new forward line; this season it is the midfield. £35million for one of the best midfielders in the league who is in his peak is the best pound-for-pound signing of a window where midfielders are moving for £100m-plus. Technical Tielemans will give United control of games from deep alongside contributing goals and assists.

The signing I'm not sure about is…

Oliver Holt: It hasn’t happened yet but if it does, I think Enzo Fernandez to Manchester City would be a mistake that would upset the balance and the ethos of the club.

Ian Herbert: Andrey Santos. A curious and very substantial £50m layout on a player who doesn’t really seem to have proved himself as a stellar talent at Chelsea. Odd summer for United.

Mike Keegan: James Trafford. I like Trafford. He’s down-to-earth, a character and clearly a talented shot-stopper. However, in this era of set-piece coaches and goals from corners, I do wonder if he has the physical presence to ensure he lives up to his £40m fee.

Riath Al-Samarrai: Sandro Tonali at Tottenham. The price tag is astronomical.

Kieran Gill: Alejandro Garnacho. Aston Villa have taken a chance on him with a loan – and a conditional obligation to buy – and he has a ton to prove.

Alejandro Garnacho remains a risky deal for Aston Villa after his uneven season in west London

Lewis Steele: Carlos Baleba to Manchester United if it happens. Brighton fans don’t seem bothered about him leaving.

Matt Barlow: Elliot Anderson. Quality player but a huge fee brings great expectation and a difficult time to join Manchester City at the end of an era.

Bobby Manzi: Luka Vuskovic. A teenage defender with a very high ceiling but £50m is a significant outlay for a centre-back who hasn’t played in the Premier League and still has plenty of development ahead of him. He will make mistakes this season - he’s young. Brighton just have to hope he fulfils his potential and eventually reaches his projected future sell-on value. After all, their model is based on calculated risks.

Manager with the most to prove

Oliver Holt: It has to be Enzo Maresca. Following Pep Guardiola is the toughest task in world football and that is Maresca’s fate. Far from universally popular at Leicester City, he left Chelsea in difficult circumstances. I’m not sure he has the personality or the people skills to lead a club of City’s size. If he does, he will join the elite of world coaching.

Ian Herbert: Enzo Maresca. The expectation will be that the prophet of Pep will simply pick up his reins, but history, his own temperament and the Community Shield tell us otherwise. Spectre of those 115 Premier League charges still a shadow on the wall.

Mike Keegan: Xabi Alonso. He got the big gig and, to say it didn’t go well, would appear to be a significant understatement. Arrives at Stamford Bridge with a big point to prove post-Real Madrid, and I think he will do just that.

Enzo Maresca is stepping into enormous shoes at the Etihad as he replaces his former boss Pep Guardiola at Man City

Riath Al-Samarrai: Enzo Maresca at Manchester City, obviously. Seemed a little too pleased with some half-decent work at Chelsea and those shoes he is filling at City are huge.

Kieran Gill: Enzo Maresca. Following Pep Guardiola is no easy task, but Manchester City paid Chelsea a total of £17m to hire him. That brings immediate pressure at a club used to winning.

Lewis Steele: Enzo Maresca. Everyone is out to get him as we saw with the vultures descending on a glorified friendly defeat against the best team in the country. He has a lot of doubters to silence. Same goes for Andoni Iraola, Xabi Alonso, the list goes on…

Matt Barlow: Enzo Maresca. Just the 15 major trophies in 10 years for Pep Guardiola, follow that.

Bobby Manzi: Alvaro Arbeloa. Arbeloa is a bit of an unknown quantity. Interim at Real Madrid for five months at the end of last season, having previously held youth roles, this is his first genuine crack at senior management. His record at Real was okay with a 64.29 per cent win rate, losing eight games. That would be more than acceptable at Fulham, not so much at Real. But he was credited for how he lifted the dressing room after a tough spell under Alonso. Fulham have enjoyed stability in recent years under Marco Silva: Arbeloa must show he can provide that.

Sports.title: Man United progressing in Carlos Baleba talks with Brighton, Aston Villa table Ollie Watkins contract offer amid Saudi interest, and Man City see Adam Wharton enquiry rebuffed: WINDOW WATCH
Sports.content:
It's that time of the year again – the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period as clubs look to make big signings ahead of the new season. Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team... Man United progressing in Baleba talks Manchester United are continuing discussions over a fee with Brighton for Carlos Baleba. Brighton have rejected United’s £60million plus £5m for the midfielder but talks have been progressing to a compromise. The 22-year-old Cameroon international is hoping the deal can be wrapped up over the weekend. Meanwhile, United right-back Habeeb Ogunneye is scheduled to undergo a medical with Arsenal ahead of his move there. The deal is understood to be a free transfer with 40percent sell-on clause. The 20-year-old is being signed to boost numbers with Arsenal’s U21s but also train with the first team. Man United have had a £65m offer for Carlos Baleba rejected but talks are progressing with Brighton Clubs circle for Jackson Atletico Madrid have enquired about a loan deal for Chelsea striker Nicolas Jackson. Atletico director Mateu Alemany was understood to have travelled to London on Thursday for talks. Jackson also has interest from Aston Villa, Napoli and Saudi Arabia. Spurs talk numbers Tottenham are working on figures with City for Savinho and forward Omar Marmoush. The deal for Savinho could be worth up to £84m. City have also asked about Crystal Palace midfielder Adam Wharton as they work through a list of targets. Leeds swoop for goalkeeper Zetterer Leeds United are closing on a deal for Eintracht Frankfurt goalkeeper Michael Zetterer to come in as James Trafford's deputy. The clubs are finalising agreement for the 31-year-old, but Frankfurt need to find a new goalkeeper to replace Zetterer first. Leeds are waiting for Lucas Perri to fully recover from a minor injury before he completes his delayed loan move to Torino. Zetterer, 31, is a former Germany U21 international. Southampton reject Villa approach for Harwood-Bellis Aston Villa have been rebuffed in an enquiry for Southampton defender Taylor Harwood-Bellis. Villa are willing to offer around £17.5m for the 24-year-old but Saints had already rejected a similar offer from Benfica. Talks are ongoing as Villa assess options such as Tosin Adarabioyo at Chelsea and Fikayo Tomori of AC Milan to fill the void left by Ezri Konsa's move to Arsenal. Villa have been rebuffed in an enquiry for Southampton defender Taylor Harwood-Bellis City keep watching brief on Wharton Manchester City maintain an interest in Crystal Palace midfielder Adam Wharton. The Selhurst Park club are reluctant to lose the 22-year-old this summer but have been making significant enquiries for midfielders in recent weeks. City are exploring several options including Manu Kone at Roma while they are advancing in talks to sign Ayyoub Bouaddi from Lille and are assessing the cost of a bid for Chelsea's Enzo Fernandez. 'We did it [sold big players in the past], and now is not the moment to do that,' said Palace boss Pierre Sage on Thursday. 'He is able to play in another club, a big club. Here, or anywhere in Europe, but one year with us, in a new dynamic, will be good for him. And we need him - that is why I think he will stay with us.' Wharton has been a significant Premier League performer in recent seasons and excelled in the Europa League Conference final but analysts at some top level would-be suitors have indicated his running statistics do not reflect someone who can fit into a high-pressing style. He continues to show on the pitch, however, an ability to find the right pass and shield his defence. City have also made contact with Palmeiras for winger Allan Elias as they seek a replacement for Savinho. Allan, 22, wants to join City but his club are reluctant to sell now with their season running to December. Talks are ongoing over a £35million fee. SIMON JONES AND BOBBY MANZI Manchester City have seen an enquiry for Adam Wharton rebuffed by Crystal Palace Jones set for Inter medical Inter Milan expect Curtis Jones to arrive later today ahead of a £30.7million move from Liverpool. The Italian side have scheduled Jones' medical for midday on Friday. Inter bid £26.7m plus £4m in add-ons with a 10 per cent sell-on clause, offering a similar structure to the deal used to sign Djed Spence from Tottenham. Curtis Jones is set to sign a five-year deal with Inter Jones, 25, will sign a five-year deal with the Serie A champions. Meanwhile, Liverpool centre back Ifeanyi Ndukwe, 18, is in talks to join Levante on loan. Ndukwe does not qualify for a work permit in England so must be loaned out. Liverpool remain in talks over PSG winger Bradley Barcola. Sheffield Wednesday are to confirm the signing of Liverpool's Northern Ireland international winger Kieran Morrison on a season-long loan. Hammers close on Mukasa West Ham are close to an agreement to sign highly-rated Manchester City forward Divine Mukasa on loan for the season. There is no buy option for the 18-year-old who spent the second half of last season on loan at Leicester City City step up hunt for Savinho replacement Manchester City have asked about Palmeiras winger Allan Elias as they consider replacements for Savinho. Allan is 22 but has not been capped by Brazil. Quick and skilful, he is not a goalscorer but has earned a reputation as a worker, willing to press. Newcastle United and Aston Villa have also scouted him in recent months. City are evaluating several options with Tottenham working on the deal to sign Savinho and forward Omar Marmoush. Bayern reach Palhinha agreement Bayern Munich have reached a full agreement with Benfica over the £17million sale of Joao Palhinha. The 31-year-old midfielder had been a target for Aston Villa and Newcastle United but will now reunite with his former Fulham boss Marco Silva at Benfica. Villa were only willing to take him on an initial loan which Bayern refused. Villa table new contract offer to Watkins Aston Villa have made a new contract offer to striker Ollie Watkins. The 30-year-old is open to a move to Al Hilal who had a £38.5m offer rejected on Tuesday but are preparing a fourth offer for the England international. Watkins has scored consistently throughout his Villa career and his goals would be difficult to replace. Villa have maintained contacts over Chelsea's Nicolas Jackson who also has interest from Napoli but he is valued around £65m. Aston Villa have put forward a new contract offer to striker Ollie Watkins Wrexham make move for ex-United star Wrexham are continuing discussions with free agent Axel Tuanzebe. The 28-year-old Congo international left Burnley at the end of last season and has had interest from clubs but is interested in Wrexham's ambitious project. Wrexham are in talks to sign former Manchester United defender Axel Tuanzebe Palace return for Auxerre target Crystal Palace have rekindled interest in Auxerre midfielder Kevin Danois. The 22-year-old was discussed as an option in January and Palace have made further enquiries. The France U21 international is an attacking player who can also play out wide and was on Newcastle United's list earlier in the year. Hull advance in talks for Betis star Garcia Hull City owner Acun Ilicali has confirmed they are making progress on their bid to sign Real Betis winger Pablo Garcia and remain in talks for Deportivo La Coruna winger Yeremay Hernandez. 'I think probably, if nothing unknown happens, we will see him in a black and gold shirt. It has to be finalised, but I would say 90 percent of this deal is done. We are talking about the last details,' said Ilicali. Pictures of Hernandez in Hull have been posted on social media, and Ilicali told BBC Humberside: 'We have to get the club side done and Yeremay also wants to come but it is a very vital, critical decision for himself. This deal is a very hard deal but we are somewhere where it looks positive. 'He is a young boy and it would change his life completely so he wanted to see where he would come. We will see in three, four days if this deal will be done or not. If it happens it will be a record for sure.' Race on for Black Cats Ta Bi West Ham and Burnley have expressed interest in Sunderland winger Jocelin Ta Bi. The 21-year-old only joined Sunderland from Maccabi Netanya in January and signed a four and a half year contract. He made one appearance in the FA Cup against Oxford United and then started against Fulham in the Premier League. As it stands, the Championship clubs have expressed interest but talks have not gone further.
