Sports.title: Brother of Finlay Tarling will ride in Vuelta a Espana just eight days after British 19-year-old was fatally struck by van during race - and parents back him with brave statement
Sports.content:
Brother of Finlay Tarling will ride in Vuelta a Espana just eight days after British 19-year-old was fatally struck by van during race - and parents back him with brave statement

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Josh Tarling will start the Vuelta a Espana this weekend just eight days after the tragic death of his brother Finlay, his team have confirmed.

Tarling has been named in Netcompany INEOS's eight-man squad for the stage race, the third and final grand tour of the season, which begins on Saturday in Monaco.

The 22-year-old will take to the start line just eight days after his younger brother Finlay, 19, died during the Tour of Portugal.

The Welsh rider died last Friday after being struck by a van during the eighth stage of the race.

Police explained earlier this week that spectators had waved the van onto the road, having thought that all the cyclists in the race had gone past.

Netcompany INEOS were the last of the 23 teams to confirm their line-up for the Vuelta a Espana, having waited for Tarling's decision on whether he wanted to participate in the three-week race following the tragedy.

Josh Tarling will start the Vuelta a Espana this weekend, just eight days after the tragic death of his brother Finlay

Finlay, 19, tragically died last Friday following a crash during the Tour of Portugal

'La Vuelta is a big opportunity for us to finish the Grand Tour season strongly.

'I'm confident in the team we're taking and their ability to adapt to whatever the race throws at us over the next three weeks. It'll be a tough race, because La Vuelta always is, but the team is united and looking forward to taking it on.

'It also goes without saying that, as a team, we all fully support Josh in his decision to take part in the race.'

Josh's decision to race has been supported by parents Michael and Dawn, who stated their son chose to race in honour of his brother.

'On Saturday Joshua will be riding the Vuelta,' Michael and Dawn wrote on Instagram.

'He has chosen to do so in honour of his brother Fin, with the full support of his family, surrounded by a team who have been incredibly supportive of whatever decision he made.

'I could not have wished for two boys who were closer growing up and into adulthood we have watched with pride as Joshua has been the most loving and supportive big brother to Fin. Following this devastating news he has been an incredible strength for us all.

'Finlay was so incredibly proud of his big brother, and would be watching nose to the tv and shouting as he competed.

Parents Dawn and Michael, pictured with Finlay, have supported Josh's decision to race

'So it is right that Josh honours that love and pride by doing what Fin always loved watching him do.'

The post was accompanied with the hashtag 'ForFin'.

A GoFundMe page, authorised by Dawn and Michael, has been set up in memory of Finlay with the aim of funding future generations of young Welsh riders.

Over £70,000 has been donated to date.

Sports.title: Harry Brook underlines his status as Test cricket's new No 1 batsman with sparkling 91, writes LAWRENCE BOOTH... as England dominate Pakistan to build a commanding lead
Sports.content:
Harry Brook underlines his status as Test cricket's new No 1 batsman with sparkling 91, writes LAWRENCE BOOTH... as England dominate Pakistan to build a commanding lead

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

The day after being confirmed as Test cricket’s new No 1 batsman, Harry Brook celebrated his ascent with a blistering 91 off 93 balls as England continued to dominate Pakistan in Leeds.

If there was disappointment at his demise, bowled by left-arm spinner Ali Usman as he closed in on what would have been his first Test hundred on his home ground, it was an innings that confirmed his panache, and took England halfway towards a welcome victory.

At stumps on the second evening, after a clatter of late wickets for Usman, they were 366 for eight, a lead of 195. Barring something unlikely, the second Joe Root era is heading for an early fillip.

Despite a moderate series against New Zealand, Brook had found himself back on top of the ICC rankings after Travis Head failed twice during Australia’s shock defeat by Bangladesh in Darwin.

Had Pakistan captain Salman Agha held on low to his right at second slip when Brook, on one, offered catching practice off Khurram Shahzad, he might have handed back his crown before it had even been measured and fitted.

But England’s vice-captain counter-attacked with brio on another rain-shortened day on which his team added 254 from 57 overs, and barely broke sweat.

Harry Brook celebrated his ascent to Test cricket’s No 1 batsman with a blistering 91 off 93 balls

Jordan Cox reacts to being dropped by the tourists - who wasted heaven-sent bowling conditions and fielded like a circus troupe

After the start was delayed until 2.45pm, there were also half-centuries for Jordan Cox, his first at this level, the inevitable Root and – on his return to the side – Dan Lawrence, as the tourists wasted heaven-sent bowling conditions and fielded like a circus troupe.

Where once Headingley drew swathes of green-shirted Pakistan fans, they are now conspicuous by their absence, a sadness that reflects their team’s fortunes. When Usman tried to field the ball with his boot on the third-man boundary and succeeded only in kicking it over the foam, you wondered what Wasim Akram or Waqar Younis must have made of it all.

If there was any criticism of England, it was a lack of ruthlessness against an attack in which only Usman and Mohammad Abbas look up to scratch. Shahzad and Muhammad Ali, by contrast, have so far taken a combined two for 200 from 38 mainly wasteful overs.

Cox played some effortless strokes in his first innings at No 3, including four boundaries in an over off Shahzad, but on 73 poked at Usman and was caught behind by Mohammad Rizwan, ending a third-wicket stand of 150. As if unable to believe what he had just done, Cox wasted a review.

So did Root four balls later, after unexpectedly missing a work to leg off Shahzad. When DRS confirmed three reds, England’s top four – including Ben Duckett on Wednesday evening – had burned all their reviews, and Root was trudging off. His dismissal pleased only the nerds: out for 66 in his 66th Test as captain, with 66 on the back of his shirt.

If Brook had been held by Agha, 198 for three would have become 205 for five, offering Pakistan a glimmer. Instead, he put on 120 in 25 overs with Lawrence, who drove straight and swept hard.

He too, though, was left with a sense of regret. Having brought up his first Test fifty in four and a half years, he miscued a slog-sweep off Usman and was walking off even as Rizwan waited for the skyer.

The stage seemed set for Brook to put aside the trauma of his 99 here a year ago against India, and he raced through the eighties. But an attempted whip to leg off Usman proved his undoing, the ball beating his outside edge and cannoning into middle stump.

Of all the treks back to the pavilion, Brook’s was the slowest, yet such has been his hold over Pakistan’s bowlers for the last four years that his performance here only marginally improved his record against them. It now reads 932 from 11 innings at nearly 85. Say what you like about the friendliness of the attack, but that is still some going.

Buoyed by the breakthrough, Usman pinned Gus Atkinson leg-before for three, then bowled Ollie Robinson first ball, celebrating a maiden five-for in only his third Test by dropping to his knees in quiet prayer.

Pakistan will need their batsmen to show similar resolve in their second innings if they are to get out of this.

Latest Curran blow leaves England short of Stokes successors

By Richard Gibson

Sam Curran’s hopes of ending a five-year Test exile next month are over after it was decided that his groin trouble requires surgery.

Curran, 28, was identified as the successor to Ben Stokes in the all-rounder role by England’s selectors and had been earmarked for a return against Pakistan at Edgbaston.

But the Surrey player, who made the last of his Test 24 appearances in August 2021, must now undergo the knife on Friday to fix a long-standing issue that kept him out of the Indian Premier League earlier this year and limited his bowling this summer.

England’s national selector Marcus North recently confirmed that Curran was lined up to feature in the third Test from 9 September pending his fitness post Hundred.

However, Curran’s disappointing news could be good for county colleague Dan Lawrence, who is currently balancing England’s team at Headingley, complementing his top-six batting with serviceable off-spin.

Ideally, England would like a seam-bowling exponent to occupy the all-rounder slot, but the lack of quality alternatives could provide Lawrence with a stay of execution in his fourth life as a Test cricketer regardless of his performances over the next fortnight.

Curran, who made the last of his Test 24 appearances in August 2021, must now undergo the knife on Friday to fix a long-standing issue that kept him out of the IPL earlier this year

Another Surrey spinning all-rounder Will Jacks, a member of last winter’s Ashes defeat, is also sidelined following an appendectomy, but unlike Curran is anticipated to be fit to face Sri Lanka in Twenty20 and one-day series in September.

England’s seam-bowling all-rounder options are limited after Jamie Overton called time on his Test career last year to concentrate on limited-overs opportunities across international and franchise scenes.

Daily Mail Sport understands there is no chance of him reconsidering this decision, but England’s apparent ditching of an obsession with pace under the new regime could be good news for his twin brother Craig when considering the third Test squad.

The last of Overton’s eight appearances came during the tour of the Caribbean in 2022, but he is having the season of his life with Somerset, hitting three hundreds with the bat and taking 33 wickets at fewer than 20 runs apiece in the County Championship.

Meanwhile, it is uncertain whether Jacob Bethell will return before the end of the season due to the meniscus issue in his knee that has ruled him out of the Pakistan series.

Bethell, 22, has established himself across all formats for England, but is currently on a strength programme for his injury with an as yet unspecified return date.

England follow the 2026 summer with a triangular white-ball tournament in Pakistan in October and a limited-overs tour of Australia in November before taking on world champions South Africa in a three-Test series spanning Christmas.

Sports.title: Matthias Jaissle urges Newcastle players to shut out 'negativity' following mass exodus of stars this summer - as new Toon boss says he 'doesn't care' about concerns over his lack of Premier League experience
Sports.content:
Matthias Jaissle has told his players to shut out the ‘negativity’ around Newcastle United ahead of their season opener against Liverpool.

After a summer in which star players such as Bruno Guimaraes, Sandro Tonali and Anthony Gordon have been sold and head coach Eddie Howe has stood down, Jaissle is aware of the outside noise forecasting a difficult season for his team.

But the German said: ‘To bring the sense of that, in the room, I think it’s smart from us to avoid the negativity from outside, and there is negativity. You read the newspapers, the media, the social media in particular.

‘So for us, the job is to focus on what we can influence. Control the controllables. This is our approach. We have a couple of days left to prepare in our best way for the match against Liverpool. We can then deliver in the best possible way at that stage.’

Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle takes charge of his first game in charge of the club on Sunday against Liverpool

Jaissle will make his Premier League managerial debut at St James’ Park on Sunday and, at 38 years old, there are some who have cast doubt on his own credentials.

'I don't know how they (people) rank us or how they rank me,’ he said. ‘To be honest, with all the respect, I don't care. It's not something I can influence, the opinion of others. We are good in our approach and we can only focus on what we can influence, and that will be the same on this whole journey with this team.’

Newcastle have signed six players so far this summer, four of whom are aged 20 or under, and Jaissle has asked for patience when it comes to judging their value during the early part of the season.

‘It’s always good when you have young players that you don’t put even more pressure from outside on them,’ he said.

‘They have already a lot of pressure and create a lot of pressure by themselves. From my side, they have full confidence and commitment and trust and respect for the journey they have ahead of them - and it would be nice if the fans and the media could see it in the same way.’

Sports.title: Inside Max Verstappen's new Red Bull contract: His astronomical salary revealed, the reason he snubbed Ferrari interest, the arguments made in tense negotiations and new deal's secret exit clause uncovered
Sports.content:
Max Verstappen has signed up to spend the best part of the remainder of his career at Red Bull for a basic salary approaching £70million a year.

The four-time world champion could earn more if the team succeeds in coming seasons. With win bonuses, his earnings would reach in excess of £100million per annum, a figure that puts him on the same footing as Lewis Hamilton at Ferrari, still Formula One’s top earner at the age of 41.

The arrangement keeps the Dutchman, 28, where he is for the next four years, extending his deal beyond 2028, his previous contract, which he previously said would be his last one.

The news comes ahead of Verstappen’s home race in the Netherlands this weekend in Zandvoort and ends interest from McLaren who were tempted by his services, as were long-time suitors Mercedes, though that dried up after the emergence of championship-leader Kimi Antonelli, the Italian wonderkid who looks likely to represent their future.

Verstappen, as revealed by Daily Mail Sport, spoke face-to-face with McLaren team principal Zak Brown in June, but the American decided to remain loyal to his world champion Lando Norris and Australian Oscar Piastri. Nor did Brown think Verstappen would quite work out there.

In truth, Verstappen wanted to remain loyal to the family that nurtured his talent, and gave him his debut at Toro Rosso, their feeder team, as a 17-year-old phenomenon.

Max Verstappen attends the announcement of his new contract at Red Bull ahead of the Dutch Grand Prix this weekend

Under the terms of his new deal, Verstappen could earn in excess of £100million a year

There were no options that held appeal in the end, and he did not much fancy Ferrari, in truth, with all its unpredictabilities.

The development also put an end to speculation that Verstappen might quit Formula One altogether, disgruntled as he is by the sport’s controversial move to half-electric engines this year.

However, it is understood that he retains a right to quit the sport, under various performance clauses, should Red Bull fail to meet his expectations over the next few years.

Verstappen revealed: ‘After the first few races, I said to Laurent (Mekies, Red Bull team principal, who took over from Christian Horner last year): “Don’t come to me with any kind of questions about the future because I don’t even know if I want to stay.”

‘Honestly, we always kept it very open.’

Verstappen and Mekies maintain very good relations, despite some friction in negotiations with Red Bull’s top brass in Salzburg, the parent soft drinks company.

Verstappen’s astute agent Raymond Vermeulen told them that his man was invaluable to them. They told him that without Red Bull, Max would not have achieved the success he has. Both of which arguments are true, though Red Bull knocked back the biggest of their star man’s pay demands.

‘He’s a lot more than the fastest driver in the world for us,' said Red Bull principal Laurent Mekies (left) of Verstappen. 'He’s the central point of the team'

Verstappen's pedigree is beyond doubt as a four-time world champion and 71-time race winner

Verstappen, a 71-time race winner, added: ‘Even if I’m not entirely happy with how the package is, I still love racing. This is still the pinnacle of motorsport, so I still want to be here.

‘I was closer to retiring than changing teams.’

Red Bull boss Mekies, for whom Verstappen’s re-signing is a major coup and which buttresses his position a year into the job, said: ‘He’s a lot more than the fastest driver in the world for us.

'He’s the central point of the team. He’s one we always refer to for all the strategic decisions we are making, and to know that he’s going to be with us in order to build that next winning cycle is phenomenal.’

Sports.title: How a billionaire is bidding to establish American football's presence in Europe with a London team the latest milestone - and what is missing to take AFL Europe to the next level
Sports.content:
How a billionaire is bidding to establish American football's presence in Europe with a London team the latest milestone - and what is missing to take AFL Europe to the next level

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

If F Scott Fitzgerald was still alive and tickling the keys of his typewriter a follow up to one of his greatest novels could have been inspired by the life and works of the American tycoon who is on a crusade to finally convert England to American football. Along with the rest of Europe.

'The Real Last Tycoon' would be the working title for an opus inspired by the life and works of American billionaire Joel Nagel.

It would be a companion work in sharp contrast to the original book in which a Hollywood executive was doomed by his lust for a movie magnate’s married daughter and thirst for the booze which hastened his demise. This sequel would be a sobering epistle on today’s board-room reality in which hard work is paramount and a supporting wife essential to corporate success.

Mr Nagel is the walking blueprint. A dedicated workaholic still able to find devoted time for his doctor wife Susan and their seven children. He toiled his way to several honours degrees in America and Germany, becoming bi-lingual in the latter.

Presides over the law firm he launched from small-town Sewickley, Pennsylvania to bestride international corporation purchases and protection of those assets. Has sat on 25 other company boards. Is head of the largest investment bank in Belize and has been ambassador for that tax haven to the United States and several European nations. Delivers life-saving community projects to impoverished third world countries. Charming too. Chuckles happily when he answers the inevitable question: ‘That’s right. Seven children and only one wife.’

All that and unassuming with it. He has taken a day trip by train from Paris for a slap-up London lunch and this rare interview. To discuss his achievements if he must but more so to talk about his passion: The American Football League Europe of which, of course, he is the boss.

Billionaire Joel Nagel is in charge of American Football League Europe, which has recently welcomed London Warriors to their eight team line-up

In particular about the London Warriors, who are the eighth and last team thus far to join the Paris Lights, Vienna Vikings, Alpine Rams, Rhein Fire, Berlin Thunder, Florence Red Lions and Wroclaw Panthers in this enterprise. To Nagel’s delight they have come from nowhere and little expectation to reach the play-offs for a place in their SuperBowl, the Gold Bowl, in Duisburg on September 6.

Perhaps only a man with such acute business acumen and legal nous to go with an entrepreneurial spirit can raise this sphinx of such a league from the ashes of five previous failures. One by the NFL itself, no less. Remember the London Monarchs and all that?

Oh, yes, and a man with the finance. One, also, who can delegate enough of his empire to his offspring. This one says: ‘I’m not ready to retire at 61 but for the first time I am in a position to give real time to my mission of establishing a sustainable American Football presence in England and most of Europe. I expect that to take five years.’

The first of those is this, the inaugural year of professional football here, for which overall losses across the league are projected at 15 million dollars. Says Nagel: ‘I expect us to break even next season. One pessimist told me that even if we succeed I may not be around long enough to enjoy the profits. Well, while this keeps me flying between homes and family I believe that this will become part of their futures.’

Crowds in Germany and Vienna have reached some 35,000 on occasion and hopes are high that will be repeated at the Gold Bowl.

Attendance for the most recent London Warriors home game was 1,500 in a day-rented ground in Ealing. But gates of three to four thousand grew through this regular season and Nagel is now negotiating for 12,000-15,000 capacity. Perhaps in Wimbledon.

‘Our fans need a home as much as our players,’ says the man who is funding wages from 500 euros a game for youngsters up-coming from their new academy to 100,000 euros a year for the stars.

This league permits the hiring of four Americans per team plus half a dozen from other European countries. But Nagel says: ‘For the game to prosper we need to develop our own players. By giving hope to them we build our ties to the local communities, which is vital for us to grow. Some of our boys come from poor backgrounds who have never travelled abroad before we arranged their passport. It gives them a real lift to get on planes to places like Paris, Berlin and Vienna.

Nagel explained how his love for the sport had come from the success of the Pittsburgh Steelers and believes the signs are there for growth in Europe

‘All this has been born of my love for the Pittsburgh Steelers. As a boy when Pennsylvania was a poor state I saw the transformation in hope and spirit brought about by the Steelers winning four SuperBowls in six years. Sports can be magical. I foresee it here with what we call soccer. I can see it forthcoming in London and England. The signs are there. In Germany and Austria the second most watched sport is American Football.

Not only do we feel a similar mood here but with all the developments in technology we are setting up now to broadcast our feed to the American market. That will help widen our sponsorships, which are strong already.

‘Our season runs from May to early September when no NFL games take place. Nor our football anywhere else.’ Only a mainstream TV deal is missing but the BBC is nibbling for next season.

Nagel is leaving no potential market untouched. This Saturday evening, against Rhein Fire, the Warriors play their last regular season game in… Mallorca. There may be a Spanish team in the offing but he adds: ‘Thousands of British holidaymakers are on that island or nearby in Spain and perhaps they will like to enjoy a family night out at The Battle Of The Beaches. We’ll see.’

To see for himself, he flew to Mallorca the morning after returning to Paris by Euro Star. As he carries on commuting to and from homes in Pennsylvania and Vienna as well all points AFL Europe he says: ‘Sometimes I think I live at 38,000 feet.’

Not unlike Scott Fitzgerald, whose Last Tycoon was left unfinished, Joel Nagel still has work to do. Hopefully, in his case, to a fulfilling conclusion.

Sports.title: Match of the Day legend fears for iconic show in major warning to BBC bosses
Sports.content:
Match of the Day legend fears for iconic show in major warning to BBC bosses

The BBC have announced more changes to Match of the Day, with the show continuing to evolve in the post-Gary Lineker era which in turn has sparked fears over its long-term future

View 2 Images Mark Lawrenson fears for Match of the Day (Image: Malcolm Couzens/Getty Images)

Match of the Day legend Mark Lawrenson has warned the BBC that the iconic show could end up suffering the same fate as Football Focus. The Beeb axed Football Focus after 52 years in May, with the corporation reshaping its football coverage.

‌



On Wednesday, chiefs announced more changes ahead of the new Premier League season, this time to its line-up for Match of the Day. Familiar faces Martin Keown, Dion Dublin, Shay Given, Stephen Warnock, Nedum Onuoha and Theo Walcott were all not named on their list of pundits, although Mirror Football understands that they will still play a role for MOTD in the 2026-27 campaign.

‌



Meanwhile, newcomers Ashley Young, Robbie Keane, Toby Alderweireld and Thomas Frank will join the show. Last season saw a new set of hosts, with Mark Chapman, Kelly Cates and Gabby Logan stepping in to replace the long-serving Gary Lineker following his abrupt departure after a fallout with BBC bosses.

‌



Assessing the state of Match of the Day four years after he exited the BBC, Lawrenson penned a column for the Telegraph. While he praised the show's new hosts, the former Liverpool defender wrote: "My worry is that there are now so many vehicles out there for the most insightful pundits - especially with the growth of podcasts such as Gary's - why would anyone feel an obligation to stay if they are worried about the direction of Match of the Day?

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



"There may come a point when questions such as, 'what is happening here?' will be asked, and other offers will feel more attractive. How long before they say, 'get me out of here?' It looks like it is already happening."

Lawrensen added: "Like all the best football shows, what attracts viewers is the familiarity of the personalities offering their insights. You may not always agree with them, but when they have authority, respect and gravitas you will still tune in to hear what they have to say."

Lineker already has a new gig, with his The Rest is Football podcast being shown on Netflix during the World Cup as part of a £14million deal, and it'll also be streamed on the platform throughout the new season. Lineker was joined in New York by ex-MOTD colleagues Alan Shearer and Micah Richards, whereas the BBC presented most of their coverage from Salford.

‌



Do you agree with Mark Lawrenson? Have your say in the comments section.

View 2 Images Mark Chapman, Gabby Logan and Kelly Cates are Match of the Day's hosts (Image: BBC)

Lawrenson labelled the decision 'nuts' and claimed that it sent a 'bad signal' to staff. "I could not believe the BBC's approach to the World Cup, with the presenting team based in Salford for the majority of the tournament while Gary and his two former BBC colleagues - Alan and Micah Richards - were in the US," the 69-year-old said.

Article continues below

"I know care has to be taken with budgets, but it's the World Cup for God's sake. That was nuts and it sends out a bad signal about priorities."

Sports.title: Man Utd's Carlos Baleba deal shows they've learnt from Frenkie de Jong mistake
Sports.content:
Man Utd's Carlos Baleba deal shows they've learnt from Frenkie de Jong mistake

Manchester United are closing in on signing Brighton's Carlos Baleba in another fast-moving piece of transfer business, unlike their days of chasing Frenkie de Jong to no avail

View 2 Images Manchester United tried to get Frenkie de Jong in 2022 (Image: Catherine Ivill/Getty Images)

No galactico signings, no tedious sagas. Is this really a Manchester United transfer window?

‌



There was plenty of noise going into the summer about United's midfield rebuild, yet they've gone about their business relatively quietly. Andrey Santos' move from Chelsea came out of the blue, while the decision to trigger Youri Tielemans' £35million release clause made for another smooth transaction.

‌



Now Carlos Baleba is in line to become United's next rapid-fire signing. Prior to Wednesday's news that the Red Devils had submitted a £65m bid, reports suggested that the Brighton midfielder was no longer a priority, with the likes of Sander Berge, Manu Kone and Aurelien Tchouameni said to be preferred.

‌



Instead, they've sprung a surprise and quickly made progress on Baleba. It's a stark contrast to how United operated in the summer of 2022 when their public pursuit of Frenkie de Jong highlighted their lacklustre transfer strategy and ended in predictable failure.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



United went about their move for De Jong in quite literal broad daylight. CEO Richard Arnold and sporting director John Murtagh - each of them no longer at the club - were spotted in Barcelona in mid-July 2022 before reaching an agreement in principle for De Jong.

That was only club-to-club, however, and the Dutchman's reluctance to join the Red Devils proved a stumbling block. BBC Sport report that even though United's recruitment staff had been told that signing De Jong was impossible, Erik ten Hag was certain it could be done, dragging out the saga for the best part of two months.

De Jong's stance never changed and after two losses in Ten Hag's first two games, United were forced to pivot. They coughed up £70m to sign a 30-year-old Casemiro and handed him a bumper four-year contract.

‌



It feels apt that in the summer Casemiro departed, the new Old Trafford hierarchy are showing that they've learned from their predecessors' mistakes. Fans have been frustrated by the lack of updates since signing Tielemans on July 14, but in reality United have worked hard to keep a low profile and maintain a stealthy approach.

Is Carlos Baleba a good signing for Manchester United? Have your say in the comments section.

View 2 Images Manchester United will have to raise their bid for Carlos Baleba (Image: Glyn KIRK/AFP via Getty Images)

‌



It should be noted that there's still work to do on Baleba, with United's offer of £60m plus £5m in add-ons not being sufficient. Nevertheless, expect the Cameroon international to be a United player by deadline day.

United did the groundwork on Baleba last summer when Brighton quoted them an eye-watering £100m off the back of his star-making season, so they'll have saved a good chunk of money by being patient. And could their latest move also serve as a blueprint for next year?

The Red Devils would also like to sign Lewis Hall, but given that Newcastle have already sold several key players this summer, it's an unlikely outcome. In 12 months' time, though, Hall will be a year closer to the expiry of his current contract and potentially more attainable.

Sports.title: Kalpana lands Yorkshire Oaks thriller but stablemate Item is team's  'first preference' for Arc
Sports.content:
Kalpana lands Yorkshire Oaks thriller but stablemate Item is team's 'first preference' for Arc

Kalpana just held on to land the Legends Global Yorkshire Oaks at York after a mighty scare from Sparan Nua in a thrilling Group One finish

View 3 Images Kalpana (left) won by a short head (Image: Richard Sellers/PA Wire)

King George heroine survived a late scare to claim the Yorkshire Oaks at York on Thursday. She was all out to thwart the dramatic late challenge of Sparan Nua in the Legends Global Yorkshire Oaks.

‌



The 10-11 favourite was made to work hard for her latest win after Aidan O'Brien's outsider Sugar Island went off in front, pulling into a 20 length lead as the field rounded the home turn.

‌



It was left to Colin Keane to chase her down from 3f out and then pass her, only for Jim Bolger's Sparan Nua – who found herself slightly hampered at one point – to eat up considerable ground and narrow the deficit.

‌



The winning post arrived just in time for Kalpana to prevail by a short head, handing Keane, Andrew Balding and owners Juddmonte a second Group One triumph within 24 hours, following Item's victory in the prestigious Juddmonte International on Wednesday.

"You knew after going a couple of furlongs it was going to be messy and passing the three (furlong marker) I thought the pacemaker was gone," said Juddmonte's European racing manager Barry Mahon.

"Colin had to commit probably a bit sooner than he wanted. When he saw himself the pacemaker was gone he had to chase her down a little bit, so she was always going to be vulnerable to something closing late, but she's gutsy and knows where the line is.

‌



View 3 Images Kalpana with the Juddmonte team at York (Image: Richard Sellers/PA Wire)

"She put her head down and got the job done. It's not pretty, but she got the job done and that's the main thing. Fast ground, slow ground, 12 furlongs - you wouldn't even be afraid to drop her back to 10. She's just very versatile and the ultimate pro now. She's fully matured now at five years of age and keeps answering all the questions, so it's wonderful."

Connections must now consider how to split their aces, with either Kalpana or Item likely to get a shot at the Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe.

‌



Should Item be given the green light to head for ParisLongchamp, Kalpana - who finished seventh in last year's Arc - will almost certainly bid to win the Qipco British Champions Fillies & Mares Stakes at Ascot later in October.

Mahon added: "We have the horse from yesterday too, so whether he'll go to the Arc and we wait for Ascot with this filly - we have to sit down in a week or two and discuss all that, but it's a nice problem to have.

View 3 Images There was a very tight finish to the Yorkshire Oaks (Image: Getty Images)

‌



"The horse from yesterday has joined the fray, so we'll decide all those sort of things in the next couple of weeks with the owners and see what they want to do.

"Item is definitely a top of the ground horse. He got away with the good to soft here yesterday. Funnily enough Colin actually said this filly doesn't enjoy the softer ground as much as she did last year, he said she felt like she enjoyed the faster ground in Ascot more the last time than she did today.

"I wouldn't have thought we'd run both in the Arc. Again that will be the owners' decision, but it wouldn't be my first preference.

Article continues below

"I suppose with Item being a colt, if the ground comes up good he'd probably have the preference, and with this filly Ascot was always the target, so it would make sense to sidestep the Arc if the ground is good - but that's a big `if'.

"She probably will retire at the end of the year. Whether she'll finish at Ascot or if she doesn't go to the Arc whether she'll go to the Breeders' Cup - there's a lot of variables to work out."

Sports.title: Mikel Arteta reveals Bruno Guimaraes injury worry in four-man Arsenal fitness update
Sports.content:
Mikel Arteta reveals Bruno Guimaraes injury worry in four-man Arsenal fitness update

Bruno Guimaraes made his Arsenal debut last Sunday by starting the Community Shield victory over Manchester City, but he's now a doubt to face Coventry on Friday night

View 2 Images Mikel Arteta has a new injury concern (Image: Stuart MacFarlane/Arsenal FC via Getty Images)

Mikel Arteta has revealed that Bruno Guimaraes is a doubt to face Coventry on Friday - while Declan Rice and Bukayo Saka are ready to start. Guimaraes, Arsenal's new £75m signing, made his debut for the Gunners when he started their 3-0 win against Manchester City in the Community Shield last Sunday.

‌



However, the Brazil international suffered a knock before being replaced by Rice at half-time. Both Rice and Saka were given additional holiday after England's long campaign at the World Cup, which came off the back of a gruelling season at club level.

‌



In his pre-match press conference on Thursday, Arteta was asked about Guimaraes and replied: "Let's see how he is. He's evolving really well, but let's see for tomorrow."

‌



There was more positive news on Rice and Saka's fitness, with the Gunners boss saying: "Yes, they're ready to be involved, yes."

One man who won't be involved is Jurrien Timber, who remains out after suffering a groin injury prior to the World Cup. Like fellow long-term absentee William Saliba, he won't be seen in the coming games.

"No, I said in the next few weeks," Arteta reiterated. "He's not training with the group yet."

Given Arsenal's current lack of depth in the backline, the Gunners are looking to sign a defender before the summer transfer window closes on September 1. Areta shouldn't have to wait too long, though, as Arsenal have agreed a £51m deal with Aston Villa to sign Ezri Konsa - although the Spaniard was coy when asked about him.

‌



"Well, we are really active in the market. I think I mentioned that a few days ago," Arteta said. "The ambition is to improve the squad.

"We have a really specific issue in the backline, especially with the long-term injury of Wilo [Saliba] and the fact that we miss one more defender; that's clear. So we are trying to reinforce that area. Whenever we're ready, we'll announce something."

He added: "I'm always positive, I'm always confident. It's something that I cannot control. It doesn't depend just on us. So we are willing to improve that area and we're going to try our best to achieve that."

In addition, Arteta confirmed that Myles Lewis-Skelly will be staying at the Emirates following speculation over his future. The 19-year-old was offered to Manchester United and Chelsea earlier this month, but Arteta declared that Lewis-Skelly will '100 per cent' be an Arsenal player beyond deadline day.

Sports.title: BBC confirm Radio Norfolk plans after outrage from ITV's Ed Balls and Mark Pougatch
Sports.content:
BBC confirm Radio Norfolk plans after outrage from ITV's Ed Balls and Mark Pougatch

The BBC has issued a statement on rumoured plans to cut Norwich City away game radio coverage on BBC Radio Norfolk

View 2 Images Mark Pougatch is not happy (Image: 2025 Visionhaus)

The BBC have moved to quash claims that it intends to axe local radio coverage of Norwich City away matches on BBC Norfolk, following a wave of backlash on social media, the Mirror can reveal. A report from the Norwich Evening News had suggested that BBC bosses were plotting to cut radio coverage of Norwich's away fixtures, sparking outrage from high-profile figures including ITV's Ed Balls and Mark Pougatch.

‌



It was claimed that BBC chiefs were planning to scale back local commentaries, meaning Chris Goreham, who provides commentary for the Canaries, would only be present at home matches. A number of prominent voices waded into the row, which has since been firmly dismissed by the BBC.

‌



ITV presenter Pougatch labelled the prospect of scrapping Norwich City away game coverage 'an absolute disgrace' if the reports proved accurate. The original article suggested Norwich City supporters would be left relying on commentary from the home side's local BBC radio station as part of efforts to save millions of pounds over the next two years.

‌



Virgil van Dijk sends clear message to Liverpool owners for final days of transfer window READ MORE :

Currently, BBC Radio Norfolk dispatches both Goreham and Rob Butler to matches, alongside a former Canary who resides near the venue. However, a BBC insider has firmly denied that any alterations to local radio coverage are on the cards.

In an official statement, the corporation said: "This is not true. Home and away game commentary, analysis and coverage will continue at BBC Radio Norfolk.

"We are looking at ways to reduce duplication and showcase more of our Local commentary teams across the BBC, but no decisions have been made. Any updates will be announced in due course."

‌



View 2 Images Local radio coverage of Norwich City away games could be scrapped. (Image: Getty)

Championship outfit Norwich, who began their campaign with a 2-1 home loss to West Brom, head to Millwall next in Saturday's 12.30pm kick-off.

The reports have sparked considerable uproar on social media, with the BBC contacting local stations to clarify the rumours were unfounded, after prominent figures slammed the corporation over the allegations.

‌



Taking to social media, Pougatch said: "I am proud to say I started my career in local radio. This would be an absolute disgrace if true. Where do I sign the petition? Local football coverage is EXACTLY the sort of thing the BBC should do. No one else will!"

The ITV presenter wasn't alone in his scathing assessment of the speculation. Former Cabinet Minister and Good Morning Britain presenter Balls also weighed in.

He said: "This can't be true - and it's not even April 1st - @CGoreham commentaries are peerless and relied upon by #ncfc fans around the world - and they are a hugely valued public service for many Norfolk based fans who can't go to games - they are what the @bbc should be all about.."

Former TNT Sports presenter and Norwich City supporter Jake Humphreys added: "This is literally what the BBC SHOULD be doing. The BBC are there for public service broadcasting. Thats exactly what this is... I hope this is an ill-founded bit of intel."

The BBC has already scrapped much-loved programmes such as Blankety Blank, Celebrity Mastermind and Live At The Apollo as the broadcaster makes "really tough choices" in a bid to save £500million over the next three years.

Bosses confirmed in June that 550 jobs would be cut and shows decommissioned. It also emerged earlier this week that the broadcaster is set to drop coverage of the World Indoor Bowls Championship as part of its ongoing cost-cutting drive, despite having aired it every year since the competition's inception in 1979.

The Boat Race has likewise departed the BBC in favour of Channel Four, while the Rugby League World Cup has returned behind a paywall for the first time since 2017, and will now be broadcast on Premier Sports.

Sports.title: Anthony Joshua told he's 'shot' ahead of Tyson Fury mega-fight
Sports.content:
Anthony Joshua told he's 'shot' ahead of Tyson Fury mega-fight

Anthony Joshua is finally set to trade leather with Tyson Fury later this year, but the former two-time heavyweight world champion's punch resistance has been brutally questioned

View Image Tyson Fury calls out Anthony Joshua

Anthony Joshua has been brutally told that his punch resistance is 'shot' ahead of his planned all-British heavyweight clash with long-time rival Tyson Fury.

‌



The pair are expected to meet in the ring later this year. While an official date and venue is yet to be announced, rumours have stated that the bout is expected to take place on November 20 at Madison Square Garden.

‌



Joshua and Fury both recently won respective tune-up fights last month. The 'Gypsy King' forced Mariusz Wach to quit in their behind-closed-doors encounter in Thailand. Joshua, on the other hand, was made to show some real adversity after being dropped twice in the opening round by Kristian Prenga. The former two-time heavyweight world champion would go on to stop the Albanian in the second stanza.

‌



Having watched Joshua in recent times, Fury's brother Shane believes 'AJ's' punch resistance is shot and insists his style falls into his brother's comfort zone. Speaking to Tony Bellew on the Fight Your Corner podcast, in partnership with Midnite , he said: “I've always felt that AJ's style fell into Tyson's comfort zone. The way Tyson used to box, okay? The man who fought Klitschko, for an example, for me, AJ wouldn't have landed a glove on him. Okay, that man now is gone. I've never seen that for years from Tyson.

FOLLOW OUR FIGHTING FB PAGE! Latest boxing and MMA news, analysis and much more via our dedicated Facebook page

‌



Tyson Fury's manager provides concerning Anthony Joshua fight update READ MORE :

Eddie Hearn issues latest Anthony Joshua vs Tyson Fury update READ MORE :

"Even though I've felt Tyson boxed well against Usyk the first time he came in light, and he boxed well, but that was probably the last time we've seen it. But I believe that's gone from Tyson. And if he can do it, I don't know if he could do it for 12 rounds. Okay. But we're looking at the stage where I believe both men are. I don't think Tyson needs to do that now."

Bellew was quick to offer his own response, stating: “Listen, what Shane just said there, I agree with it 100 times over. That version of Tyson Fury that got in with Klitschko, the one that can move for 12 rounds, that can nullify you and negate you. No, AJ is not going to beat him. I agree, and I said this before. I don't want to comment anymore on Tyson and on AJ and Fury because you don't know if it's happening. I'm sick of it. You don't know which fighter stands where. And I said one thing I will say is this: this is the best chance AJ's ever had of beating Tyson Fury right now.”

Fury added: “Yeah, I'd say so. But the issue is after the Makhmudov fight, after the fight, I've done 10 interviews afterwards, and I said quite clearly on you. I said the stage where they are now because, even though that was a good performance for Tyson, it was a solid performance, but that was not a vintage Tyson performance.”

Article continues below

Tyson Fury drops biggest Anthony Joshua fight hint yet after ultimatum READ MORE :

After watching his brother's comeback win over Arslanbek Makhmudov back in April, Fury is confident that the 'Gypsy King' will win his monumental meeting with Joshua. “I think all heavyweight men can punch. I've never come across one who can't punch, and I also believe that there's a difference in power. You can have a really good knockout man at British level, and when he steps up, he's not a puncher at all. I think, from punch resistance, I think AJ is shot," he said.

"If he hits you before you hit him, you're done. And we're not under any illusions with that. Listen, he's a good, good finisher. He can put his punches together. Listen, he's a two-time world champion. But I just feel that I put the fight originally as a 50/50. But after Makhmudov, I just think that Tyson's going to hit him. And what we've seen in the last two proper fights, when he gets hit with a solid shot, you see something happen, he doesn't have to be knocked down or knocked on the floor, but you can see a reaction. So yeah, we're confident. Is the fight happening too late? Probably is.”

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."

Collins: Ireland must build on World Cup near miss

Ireland captain Nathan Collins is confident his side have laid the foundations to qualify for future tournaments having seen hopes of reaching this summer's World Cup finals come to an end.

Collins and his team-mates were agonisingly close to the play-off final when they led the Czech Republic 2-1 in Prague on Thursday evening with just four minutes of normal time remaining.

Image: A dejected Nathan Collins and head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson

However, Czech skipper Ladislav Krejci's late equaliser took the tie to extra-time and ultimately to penalties, where the hosts prevailed 4-3 to extend Ireland's wait for a first return to the big stage since 2002.

Asked about their progression to the play-offs, which was secured by back-to-back wins over Armenia, Portugal and Hungary, Brentford defender Collins said: "I'm not seeing many positives right now because we're in the gutter.

"But what we've created, the environment created with the fans and country, has been special. That's something we need to keep growing, to get even better at.

"That can help us get better on the pitch. We can push that and get fans to more tournaments."

Ireland had hoped to return to the Aviva Stadium on Tuesday for a showdown with either Denmark or North Macedonia for a place in the finals, but the Czechs will now host the Danes, who were 4-0 winners in Copenhagen.

Instead, Heimir Hallgrimsson's side face a friendly against the Macedonians.

Collins said: "The motivation has to be the same. We've to win to keep improving as a team and country. Any game we play at home is a big game."

Sports.title: 'Pain' - Irish heartbreak as Czech Republic win on penalties
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland's World Cup hopes were cruelly and heartbreakingly dashed as Czech Republic came from 2-0 down - to then beat them on penalties.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, who went two goals up after 23 minutes in Prague, were four minutes plus stoppage-time away from victory - before Wolves defender Ladislav Krejci headed in a corner to force extra-time.

Ireland were also a handful of penalties away from going through, as penalty saving expert Caomhin Kelleher saved from Mojmír Chytil in the shoot-out to give them a momentary advantage.

But Finn Azaz and Alan Browne both missed their spot kicks, allowing Patrick Schick and then Jan Kliment to win it for the hosts.

As a result, Czech Republic will go on to face Denmark on Tuesday for a spot at the World Cup - as Ireland's wait for a first World Cup appearance since 2002 goes on.

After Wales and Northern Ireland's semi-final exits, it also means England and Scotland will be the only teams from Great Britain and Ireland at the World Cup this summer.

Image: Ireland's players walk off the pitch after defeat

World Cup play-off finals - Europe Bosnia & Herzegovina vs Italy

Sweden vs Poland

Kosovo vs Turkey

Czech Republic vs Denmark

How Ireland threw away their lead

Ireland came flying out the blocks flying in Prague. Four shots in the opening ten minutes, including Nathan Collins crashing a shot off the bar from range, set the tone for a brilliant display - and they got their rewards.

A long throw caused chaos and Nathan Collins was deemed to have been caught slightly late by Vladimir Darida by VAR, who sent referee Glenn Byberg to the monitor for a review.

Troy Parrott, who else, crashed in the penalty for his sixth goal in the last three Ireland matches. And it got better for Ireland four minutes later.

Ryan Manning's corner found Dara O'Shea at the back post and his header across was cleared off the line by Vladimir Coufal - but off goalkeeper Matej Kovar and over the line.

Image: Czech Republic goalkeeper Matej Kovar scores an own goal to give Ireland a 2-0 lead

Ireland were in dreamland but a moment of Manning madness brought the Czech Republic back into it. The defender's needless tug back on Krekci - when the ball was heading out of play - was penalised by referee Byberg, with Patrick Schick pulling one back from the spot.

Ireland did, however, manage to settle the nerves down - right throughout the second half. Despite sustained Czech pressure in the second half, they barely threatened.

It was Ireland who had the better chances after the break, with Jayson Molumby striking the post and Parrott denied by a solid Kovar save at a corner. But then heartbreak struck with four minutes of normal time remaining, as Krejci bundled the ball in at the near post from a set piece.

Krejci could have even won it with the last kick of the game but scuffed his finish, as extra-time came.

Substitute Tomas Soucek missed a glorious chance for the hosts, with Adam Idah was denied a one-on-one chance by a goal-saving challenge from Stepan Chaloupek. Penalties came and the lottery fell in the hosts' favour.

Image: Jan Kliment scored the winning goal in the penalty shoot-out

Hallgrimsson confident in Ireland future despite 'pain'

Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson:

"One word is pain. I feel pain. I feel pride for the performance of the players. They gave it all. I feel gratitude for all the supporters who supported us through the whole game, even after the loss. I feel pride being a part of that group. Personally, I know all the players will feel pain now. Only pain.

"We take with us that we can play teams higher in the FIFA ranking and can punch above our weight: Portugal, Hungary and here. We can compete with these teams. We came here with three wins in a row, a long time since that happened for this national team.

"So there's growth in this squad. It's maturing. These are been the biggest game most of these players have played. That's encouraging to know we're growing. It's strange to say that after we lost today.

"I know I'm biased in this, all the statistics and metrics of the team have improved. Big games, being on the line, crunch times all the time, we've managed to go through this. It showed the resilience, character of these players, that's why I feel confident going on."

Sports.title: Wilson key for Wales, NI aim for big upset while history beckons for ROI
Sports.content:
Sky Sports assesses Thursday's 2026 World Cup play-off semi-finals as Wales host Bosnia-Herzegovina, Northern Ireland go to four-time winners Italy and the Republic of Ireland face Czech Republic in Prague.

Thursday 7.45pm: Wales vs Bosnia-Herzegovina (winner will play Italy or Northern Ireland)

Harry Wilson is not the new Gareth Bale, but he's doing the job of Bale at his best, especially for Wales.

Fans have long been excited about Wilson's natural talent, but are now seeing his influence in the Premier League on a weekly basis for Fulham. This season, he has 10 goals and six assists for club, while for country, his stats are even better with five goals and two assists in his last five games.

If Wilson starts running the show, his confidence will feed to the other players and to the home crowd, and Wales will be very difficult to stop on their own patch.

Which World Cup group would Wales be in? If Wales qualify for the World Cup they would be in Group B with Canada, Switzerland and Qatar.

Craig Bellamy wanted to create an identity for Wales when he took over as head coach. It's now clear: he wants front-foot football coupled with intensity and energy.

Bellamy doesn't always see that in international football as he finds it slower at times compared with club football, but his Wales side will not be ponderous. You could see during the qualification campaign that Wales' intensity in winning the ball back very quickly and holding possession grew. Now it's about consistently doing it.

Apart from consistency in play, there needs to be consistency in selection. Much is always made about the 'spine' of a good team, from the goalkeeper to the glory hunter! Leeds United provide a fair chunk of Wales' spine with 'keeper Karl Darlow on form and in receipt of the No.1 keeper's jersey. Joe Rodon is the rock at centre-back that success relies upon, while team-mate Ethan Ampadu's versatility means he can link anywhere between defence and midfield. Throw in one of the in-form Premier League stars, Harry Wilson, and a strong spine can take a team a long way.

Ask Bellamy if he has thought about preparing for the play-off final against either Italy or Northern Ireland and you'll get glared at. It's Bosnia, Bosnia and Bosnia. He won't entertain anything beyond Bosnia until the game is over. It's a danger, a banana skin he wants to avoid. Thinking too far ahead isn't good on this occasion.

Geraint Hughes

Thursday 7.45pm: Italy vs Northern Ireland (winner will play Wales or Bosnia-Herzegovina)

On paper, perhaps in reality, it's David vs Goliath.

Northern Ireland enjoy David vs Goliath. Once upon a time it was David (Healy) vs England and David (Healy) vs Spain.

For smaller nations there is comfort in being the underdog. A loss would be met without a major backlash, a win makes you a hero. That's how Michael O'Neill's side will approach Thursday's assignment in Bergamo against Italy.

Which World Cup group would Northern Ireland be in? If Northern Ireland qualified for the World Cup they would be in Group B with Canada, Switzerland and Qatar.

Conor Bradley and Daniel Ballard are out. Between them they represent 50 per cent of the Northern Ireland players currently plying their trade in the Premier League.

The pair's absence is as much a blow to Northern Ireland's attacking prospects as it is defensively. Ballard represents their best aerial threat from set-pieces, Bradley their most dynamic player on the ball.

And yet for some reason that only football can explain, hope remains. The four-time World Cup winners are heavy favourites but far from the Azzurri powerhouse of old.

If Northern Ireland have it their way, it's unlikely to be a pretty spectacle. But can they frustrate their hosts? 0-0 at half-time? Pounce on the sense of angst that will exist among the home support?

To call it a free hit would be to downplay the importance of the game. But Northern Ireland are free from the weight of expectation.

Daring to dream of a result that becomes instant folklore.

Michael Morrow

Thursday 7.45pm: Czech Republic vs Republic of Ireland (winner will play Denmark or North Macedonia)

Image: Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson and captain Seamus Coleman spoke to the media in Prague

History beckons for the Republic of Ireland here in Prague.

Make no mistake, this will be the biggest game to date for a lot of these Irish players as they attempt to take another step to this summer's World Cup but they must get past Czech Republic to do so.

Which World Cup group would Republic of Ireland be in? If the Republic of Ireland qualified for the World Cup they would be in Group A with co-hosts Mexico, South Africa and South Korea.

Still coming off the euphoria of the incredible back-to-back wins against Portugal and Hungary last November, this is an Irish team full of confidence.

Having spoken to a few people around the Czech Republic team, those results have been noted and they are particularly worried about Irish striker Troy Parrott, who scored five goals in those two games in November - including the 96th-minute winner against Hungary.

Head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson spoke ahead of this game about one of the key aspects is visually and mentally being ready for the challenge ahead of them, he seemed as calm and confident as usual.

However his key selection dilemma is does he bring back the experienced, tried and tested players such as Seamus Coleman, Robbie Brady and Chiedoze Ogbene - all three have had limited game-time this season for a variety of injuries.

Coleman and Brady especially are the only two players in the squad who were part of Ireland's last team in a major tournament which was in 2016 - their experience could prove vital.

Image: Can Troy Parrott recreate his Irish heroics in Prague on Thursday?

Their opponents are in a state of flux.

Czech Republic have a new head coach who takes charge of his first game on Thursday, with West Ham's Tomas Soucek also being stripped of the captaincy after November's internationals having caused shockwaves in the local media - Wolves' Ladislav Krejci has replaced him.

The pressure feels like it's all on the home side which could play into Ireland's advantage as they look to take another step to qualify for this summer's World Cup - their first since 2002.

Danyal Khan
